children.translated_text: Like word and meaning inseparably joined, for the apprehension of word and meaning,
I salute the parents of the world, <s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>. // 1.1 //

children.text: kva sūryaprabhavo vaṃśaḥ kva cālpaviṣayā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: How great is the dynasty born of the Sun! How limited is my intellect!
Desiring to cross the uncrossable ocean, I am foolishly setting out in a raft. // 1.2 //
Dull-witted yet aspiring to the fame of poets, I shall become an object of ridicule,
Like a dwarf reaching up his arms in greed for a fruit attainable only by the tall. // 1.3 //
Or rather, in this dynasty where earlier poets have made an opening of words,

children.text: maṇau vajrasamutkīrṇe sūtrasyevāsti me gatiḥ // Ragh(K)_1.4 //
children.translated_text: I have a passage like a thread through a gem already pierced by diamond. // 1.4 //
Thus I, of those pure from birth, whose deeds bore fruit until the end,
who were lords of the earth extending to the oceans, whose chariots traveled roads reaching to the sea, // 1.5 //
who offered oblations to the fire according to prescribed rites, who honored supplicants according to their desires,
who punished the guilty according to their offenses, who rose according to the proper time, // 1.6 //
who accumulated wealth only for giving it away, who spoke sparingly for the sake of truth,
who desired conquests only for glory, who were householders only for the sake of progeny, // 1.7 //
who in childhood mastered learning, who in youth pursued the objects of sense,
who in old age adopted the ways of ascetics, and who at the end relinquished their bodies through <s>yoga</s>, // 1.8 //
shall narrate the lineage of the <s>Raghus</s>, though my powers of speech are slender,
for their virtues, reaching my ears, have beguiled me into rashness. // 1.9 //
Let the virtuous deign to hear this, for they are the judges that distinguish good from bad;

children.text: hemnaḥ saṃlakṣyate hyagnau viśuddhiḥ śyāmikāpi vā // Ragh(K)_1.10 //
children.translated_text: indeed, in fire is discerned the purity of gold, or its impurity as well. // 1.10 //
There was one named <s>Manu</s>, son of <s>Vivasvat</s>, worthy of honor among the wise,
the first among kings of the earth, as the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> is among the Vedic meters. // 1.11 //
In that lineage of great purity was born one of still greater purity,
<s>Dilīpa</s> by name, a moon among kings, like the moon risen from the ocean of milk. // 1.12 //
Broad-chested, bull-shouldered, tall as a <s>Śāla</s> tree, mighty-armed,

children.text: ātmakarmakṣamaṃ dehaṃ kṣātro dharma ivāśritaḥ // Ragh(K)_1.13 //
children.translated_text: he had assumed a body fit for his duties, as if the <s>Kṣatriya</s> <s>dharma</s> itself had taken bodily form. // 1.13 //
With a substance surpassing all, with a splendor overpowering all,
he stood supreme over the earth, like <s>Meru</s> having traversed the world by its own eminence. // 1.14 //
His wisdom matched his appearance, his learning matched his wisdom,
his undertakings matched his learning, and his success matched his undertakings. // 1.15 //
Through his kingly virtues, both awe-inspiring and gracious, he was to his dependents
both unapproachable and accessible, like the ocean with its precious gems. // 1.16 //
Not even by a hair's breadth beyond the well-trodden path of their king
did his subjects ever stray, their conduct governed as if by the rim of a wheel. // 1.17 //
He collected taxes from his subjects solely for their welfare;
for the sun draws up moisture only to release it a thousandfold. // 1.18 //
His army and his treasury were but two means of accomplishing his ends;

children.text: śāstre ca vyāpṛtā buddhirmaurvī dhanuṣi cātatā // Ragh(K)_1.19 //
children.translated_text: his intellect was devoted to the <s>śāstras</s> (sacred sciences), and his bowstring was ever strung upon the bow. // 1.19 //
His counsels were kept secret, his expressions and gestures concealed,

children.text: phalānumeyāḥ prārambhāḥ saṃskārāḥ prāktanā iva // Ragh(K)_1.20 //
children.translated_text: and his undertakings could be inferred only from their results, like the <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) of a former life. // 1.20 //
He guarded himself without fear, he practiced <s>dharma</s> without distress,
he acquired wealth without greed, and he enjoyed pleasures without attachment. // 1.21 //

children.text: jñāne maunaṃ kṣamā śaktau tyāge ślāghāviparyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Silence in his knowledge, forbearance in his strength, absence of self-praise in his generosity --
his virtues seemed born together, each naturally accompanied by its kindred quality. // 1.22 //
Undrawn by the objects of sense, having seen beyond all branches of learning,
his was an elder's maturity without old age, for he was devoted to <s>dharma</s>. // 1.23 //
Through instilling discipline in his subjects, through protecting them, and through nourishing them,

children.text: sa pitā pitarastāsāṃ kevalaṃ janmahetavaḥ // Ragh(K)_1.24 //
children.translated_text: he was their true father; their natural fathers were merely the cause of their birth. // 1.24 //
He punished the guilty for the sake of social order, he married for the sake of progeny;

children.text: apyarthakāmau tasyāstāṃ dharma eva manīṣiṇaḥ // Ragh(K)_1.25 //
children.translated_text: even <s>artha</s> (wealth) and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure) were, for that wise one, subservient to <s>dharma</s> alone. // 1.25 //

children.text: dudoha gāṃ sa yajñāya sasyāya maghavā divam /
children.translated_text: He milked the earth for <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), and <s>Maghavat</s> (Indra) milked heaven for crops;
through this mutual exchange of bounties, the two sustained both worlds. // 1.26 //
Other kings did not rival his fame as protector, indeed;

children.text: vyāvṛttā yatparasvebhyaḥ śrutau taskaratā sthitā // Ragh(K)_1.27 //
children.translated_text: for having turned away from others' possessions, the very notion of thievery remained only in the <s>Vedas</s> (as a word in scripture). // 1.27 //
Even a hateful person, if virtuous, was accepted by him, like bitter medicine by the afflicted;
even a beloved person, if wicked, was cast off, like a finger bitten by a serpent. // 1.28 //
Surely the Creator fashioned him with the concentration used for the great elements;

children.text: tathā hi sarve tasyāsanparārthaikaphalā guṇāḥ // Ragh(K)_1.29 //
children.translated_text: for indeed, all his virtues bore fruit solely for the benefit of others. // 1.29 //
The earth, girdled by its shores as by a bracelet, with the ocean made its moat,
under no other's command -- he ruled it as if it were a single city. // 1.30 //
His wife, born of the <s>Magadha</s> lineage, was fittingly named
<s>Sudakṣiṇā</s>, by a name befitting her grace, like the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) to a sacrifice. // 1.31 //
Though he had a vast inner palace, the lord of the earth considered himself truly wedded

children.text: tayā mene manasvinyā lakṣmyā ca vasudhādhipaḥ // Ragh(K)_1.32 //
children.translated_text: only through that spirited woman and through <s>Lakṣmī</s> (royal fortune). // 1.32 //
In her, who was worthy of him, eager for the birth of a son,

children.text: vilambitaphalaiḥ kālaṃ sa nināya manorathaiḥ // Ragh(K)_1.33 //
children.translated_text: he passed the time with hopes whose fruits were long delayed. // 1.33 //
Like <s>Bhagīratha</s> once entrusted the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, capable of purifying his ancestors,

children.text: īpsatā santatiṃ nyastā tena mantriṣu kosalā // Ragh(K)_1.34 //
children.translated_text: so he, desiring progeny, entrusted <s>Kosalā</s> (his kingdom) to his ministers. // 1.34 //
Then, having worshipped the Creator, devout and desirous of a son,
the royal couple went to the <s>āśrama</s> (hermitage) of their guru <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. // 1.35 //
Mounted upon a single chariot whose rumble was deep and gentle,
they were like <s>Vidyut</s> (Lightning) and <s>Airāvata</s> upon a rain cloud of the monsoon season. // 1.36 //
With a measured retinue, lest the hermitage be burdened,
they were like a pair of tamed elephants followed by only a few fragrant young calves. // 1.37 //
They were attended by breezes pleasant to the touch, fragrant with the resin of <s>Śāla</s> trees,
scattering flower pollen, stirring the rows of forest trees. // 1.38 //
Because the wind was favorable -- an omen foretelling the fulfillment of their prayer --
the dust raised by the horses did not touch their hair ornaments. // 1.39 //
Accepting fresh butter from the elders of the cowherding settlements who came to greet them,
they asked the names of the trees along the forest path. // 1.40 //
They inhaled the fragrance of lotuses in the lakes, cooled by the agitation of waves,
a fragrance that seemed to imitate their own sighs. // 1.41 //
They listened to the enchanting cries of peacocks, drawn by the sound of the chariot wheels,

children.text: ṣaḍjasaṃvādinīḥ kekā dvidhā bhinnāḥ śikhaṇḍibhiḥ // Ragh(K)_1.42 //
children.translated_text: whose calls, split in two, harmonized with the <s>ṣaḍja</s> note. // 1.42 //
In pairs of deer that had not strayed far from the path,
they saw a resemblance to each other's eyes, as the deer gazed fixedly at the chariot. // 1.43 //
At times they lifted their faces upward toward <s>Sārasa</s> cranes whose melodious cries
wove garlands for an archway without pillars, extending from their rows in flight. // 1.44 //
In villages they themselves had granted to the sacrificers, marked by sacrificial posts,
they received unfailing offerings of <s>arghya</s> (water of welcome) and blessings at every step. // 1.45 //
An indescribable radiance belonged to those two as they traveled in pure attire,
like <s>Citrā</s> (the star) and the Moon when freed from winter haze and conjoined. // 1.46 //
The king, pleasing to behold, showing his queen each place of interest,

children.text: api laṅghitamadhvānaṃ bubudhe na budhopamaḥ // Ragh(K)_1.47 //
children.translated_text: did not even notice that the journey had been traversed, so wise was he like <s>Budha</s> (Mercury). // 1.47 //
He of hard-won fame reached the hermitage with wearied horses,
at evening, accompanied by his queen, to the abode of that great sage of restrained senses. // 1.48 //
It was being filled with ascetics returning from the forest's interior, bearing kindling and <s>kuśa</s> grass on their shoulders,
purified by coming forth to meet the sacred fires. // 1.49 //
Its trees had been left undisturbed by the sage's daughters after watering,
for the comfort of the birds that drank from the water-basins at their roots. // 1.50 //
On the grounds before the leaf-huts, where wild rice had been spread to dry in the sun by the <s>Niṣāda</s> women,
deer were chewing their cud. // 1.51 //
It was filled with deer blocking the doorways of the leaf-huts of the sages' wives,
like their own children, accustomed to their share of wild rice. // 1.52 //
It was purifying those approaching the hermitage with its smoke,
stirred by the wind, fragrant with oblations, revealing the rekindled fires. // 1.53 //
Then, instructing the charioteer to rest the draft horses,
he helped his wife descend from the chariot and descended himself. // 1.54 //
To him who came with his wife, the protector with fully subdued senses,
the sages, courteous and wise in statecraft, offered due honors to that one worthy of worship. // 1.55 //
At the conclusion of the evening rites, he beheld that treasury of <s>tapas</s> (austerity),
attended by <s>Arundhatī</s>, like the oblation-consuming fire attended by <s>Svāhā</s>. // 1.56 //

children.text: tayorjagṛhatuḥ pādau rājā rājñī ca māgadhī /
children.translated_text: The king and the queen of <s>Magadha</s> lineage clasped their feet;

children.text: tau gururgurupatnī ca prītyā pratinanandatuḥ // Ragh(K)_1.57 //
children.translated_text: the guru and the guru's wife joyfully welcomed them in return. // 1.57 //
The host, that sage dwelling in the <s>āśrama</s> of kingship, once the guest's fatigue from the journey had been soothed by hospitality,

children.text: papraccha kuśalaṃ rājye rājyāśramamuniṃ muniḥ // Ragh(K)_1.58 //
children.translated_text: inquired after the welfare of the kingdom. // 1.58 //
Then, before that treasury of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, he who had conquered his enemies' cities,
the lord of wealth, the best of speakers, spoke these meaningful words. // 1.59 //

children.text: upapannaṃ nanu śivaṃ saptasvaṅgeṣu yasya me /
children.translated_text: "Is it not natural that all is well with me in the seven limbs of my kingdom,

children.text: daivīnāṃ mānuṣīṇāṃ ca pratikartā tvamāpadām // Ragh(K)_1.60 //
children.translated_text: since you are the one who averts calamities both divine and human? // 1.60 //
By your <s>mantras</s>, O performer of sacred rites, my enemies are subdued from afar;

children.text: pratyādiśyanta iva me dṛṣṭalakṣyabhidaḥ śarāḥ // Ragh(K)_1.61 //
children.translated_text: my arrows, which strike their visible targets, seem almost put to shame. // 1.61 //
The oblation duly offered by you, the <s>hotṛ</s> (priest), into the sacred fires,
becomes rain for the crops that were withering in drought. // 1.62 //
Living the full span of human life, free from disease, free from calamity --
that my subjects are so, the cause is your <s>brahmavarcas</s> (brahmanical splendor). // 1.63 //
Thus being watched over by a guru born of <s>Brahman</s> himself,

children.text: sānubandhāḥ kathaṃ na syuḥ sampado me nirāpadaḥ // Ragh(K)_1.64 //
children.translated_text: how could my fortunes not be enduring and free from misfortune? // 1.64 //
Yet in this bride of yours, I have not seen progeny worthy of her;

children.text: na māmavati sadvīpā ratnasūrapi medinī // Ragh(K)_1.65 //
children.translated_text: the earth, though possessing continents, though a mine of gems, does not satisfy me. // 1.65 //
Thinking that what lies beyond me is hard to attain, surely my ancestors, won over by me,
drink their offered milk rendered lukewarm by their own sighs. // 1.66 //
Thus I, though my soul is purified by sacrifice, am veiled by the loss of progeny,
like the mountain <s>Lokāloka</s>, which is both light and darkness. // 1.67 //
The happiness of the next world, being meritorious, arises from <s>tapas</s> (austerity) and charity;

children.text: santatiḥ śuddhavaṃśyā tu paratreha ca śarmaṇe // Ragh(K)_1.68 //
children.translated_text: but offspring of a pure lineage bring happiness both here and hereafter. // 1.68 //

children.text: tayā hīnaṃ vinetā māṃ kathaṃ paśyanna dūyate /
children.translated_text: How can you, my guide, see me deprived of that and not grieve,
as though you yourself had lovingly watered a barren tree in the hermitage? // 1.69 //
Know, O venerable one, this bond of ancestral debt that causes me unbearable pain,
like a tethering post that chafes a newly bound elephant." // 1.70 //
"Therefore, please arrange things so that I may be freed;

children.text: ikṣvākūṇāṃ durāpe 'rthe tvadadhīnā hi siddhayaḥ // Ragh(K)_1.71 //
children.translated_text: for the fulfillment of goals hard to attain for the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> depends upon you." // 1.71 //
Thus informed by the king, the sage stood still for a moment
with eyes closed in meditation, like a lake whose fish have fallen asleep. // 1.72 //
Through his meditative insight, that realized soul perceived the cause of the obstruction of progeny
for the lord of the earth, and then enlightened him. // 1.73 //
"Previously, when you were returning to earth after attending upon <s>Śakra</s> (Indra),
<s>Surabhī</s> (the divine cow) was on the path, resting in the shade of the <s>Kalpataru</s> (wish-fulfilling tree). // 1.74 //
Thinking of this divine cow, who had just bathed after her season, you hurried past
without performing the rite of circumambulation, and aroused her anger. // 1.75 //
'Since you disregard me, you shall have no offspring;

children.text: matprasūtimanārādhya prajeti tvā śaśāpa sā // Ragh(K)_1.76 //
children.translated_text: without first propitiating my daughter, you shall have no progeny' -- thus she cursed you. // 1.76 //

children.text: sa śāpo na tvayā rājanna ca sārathinā śrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: That curse was not heard by you, O king, nor by your charioteer,
for the celestial elephant was trumpeting loudly in the current of the heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>. // 1.77 //
I understand that your desire, hindered by that transgression, requires effort to fulfill;
for failure to honor the venerable obstructs one's welfare. // 1.78 //
She now resides in <s>Pātāla</s> (the netherworld), whose entrance is guarded by serpents,
providing <s>havis</s> (oblation-milk) for the long sacrificial session of <s>Pracetas</s>. // 1.79 //
Therefore, you, together with your wife, should propitiate her daughter, my own cow and mother of calves,

children.text: ārādhaya sapatnīkaḥ sā vāṃ kāmaṃ pradāsyati // Ragh(K)_1.80 //
children.translated_text: who is one generation removed from <s>Surabhī</s>; she will grant your wish." // 1.80 //
Even as he was speaking thus, the means of the priest's oblation,

children.text: anindyā nandinī nāma dhenurāvavṛte vanāt // Ragh(K)_1.81 //
children.translated_text: the blameless cow named <s>Nandinī</s>, returned from the forest. // 1.81 //
Bearing a coppery streak born on her forehead, she with her dark and light coloring
resembled the twilight of the first lunar day, streaked by the crescent moon. // 1.82 //
With udders warm and full, she rained upon the ground with her dripping milk,
purer even than the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding sacrificial bath), prompted by the sight of her calf. // 1.83 //
The dust particles kicked up by her hooves, touching the king's body from nearby,
bestowed upon him a purity equal to that of bathing at a sacred <s>tīrtha</s> (pilgrimage site). // 1.84 //
Seeing her, auspicious to behold, the knower of omens, that treasury of <s>tapas</s> (austerity),
spoke again to his sacrificer, whose prayers had never been fruitless:
"O King, consider that success is not far from you;

children.text: upasthiteyaṃ kalyāṇī nāmni kīrtita eva yat // Ragh(K)_1.86 //
children.translated_text: this auspicious one has arrived — for she is <s>Kalyāṇī</s> (the Auspicious) even in name."
"You should propitiate this cow, who lives on forest fare, by constantly following her,
as one would master a <s>vidyā</s> (branch of knowledge) through diligent practice."
"When she sets forth, you should set forth; when she stands still, you should stand;
when she sits down, you should sit beside her; when she has drunk water, you should drink water."
"And let your wife, devoted in her service, having honored this cow from the <s>tapovana</s> (ascetic grove),
follow her as she goes forth in the morning and come out to meet her in the evening."
"Thus, through her grace, be devoted to her service;

children.text: avighnamastu te stheyāḥ piteva dhuri putriṇām // Ragh(K)_1.90 //
children.translated_text: may there be no obstacle for you — you must stand firm in the yoke of parenthood, as a father does for his children."
"So be it" — with these words, the delighted one, free from possessions,
accepted the command — a disciple who knew time and place, bowing before his preceptor.

children.text: atha pradoṣe doṣajñaḥ saṃveśāya viśāṃ patim /
children.translated_text: Then at nightfall, the knower of faults, the son of the Creator who speaks pleasant words,
dismissed the lord of people, resplendent in glory, for his rest.
Though the <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) was already his, the sage, out of regard for proper observance,
being versed in ritual propriety, ordained for him only forest provisions.
Having occupied the leaf-hut assigned by the <s>kulapati</s> (head of the hermitage), accompanied only by his dutiful wife,

children.text: tacchiṣyādhyayananiveditāvasānāṃ saṃviṣṭaḥ kuśaśayane niśāṃ nināya // Ragh(K)_1.94 //
children.translated_text: he lay down upon a bed of <s>kuśa</s> grass and passed the night, whose end was announced by the recitations of the sage's pupils.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>sarga</s> (canto) of the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem).

children.translated_text: Then at dawn, the lord of his people, the glory-wealthy one, released the sage's cow toward the forest,
her calf having been tied after she had been milked, and having received garlands and fragrant offerings from his wife.
The royal consort, worthy of being celebrated foremost among the stainless, followed in her path,
the dust of which was sanctified by the cow's hoof-prints, as <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition) follows the meaning of <s>Śruti</s> (revelation).

children.text: nivartya rājā dayitāṃ dayālustāṃ saurabheyīṃ surabhiryaśobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The compassionate king, having turned back his beloved, tended that daughter of <s>Surabhī</s>, glorious in splendor,
as though she were the earth in the form of a cow, with the four oceans as her udders.
For the sake of his vow, only a single attendant was permitted to accompany the cow; the rest of the retinue was forbidden,

children.text: na cānyatastasya śarīrarakṣā svavīryaguptā hi manoḥ prasūtiḥ // Ragh(K)_2.4 //
children.translated_text: nor was any other protection needed for his person, for the offspring of <s>Manu</s> was guarded by his own valor.
With flavorful mouthfuls of grass, with scratching to relieve her itches, with warding off biting flies,
and with unhindered freedom of movement, the sovereign was wholly intent on propitiating her.
Standing still when she stood, moving when she moved, sitting with patient composure when she sat down,

children.text: jalābhilāṣī jalamādadānāṃ chāyeva tāṃ bhūpatiranvagacchat // Ragh(K)_2.6 //
children.translated_text: reaching for water when she desired water — the king followed her like a shadow.
Though he had set aside the insignia of royalty, he bore a royal majesty discerned by his extraordinary radiance,
like a lordly elephant in the state of inner <s>mada</s> (rut), its temple-streaks not yet visible.
With his hair entangled in trailing creepers, his bow strung, he roamed the forest,
as if seeking out dangerous beasts under the pretext of guarding his guru's sacrificial cow.
The trees flanking his path, like those standing beside <s>Yama</s> (the god of death) who bears the noose,
seemed to announce his approach with the cries of birds startled from their perches.
And young creepers, swayed by the wind, showered blossoms upon him
as he approached majestically like a friend of the wind-god — like city maidens casting ceremonial parched rice.
The doe-eyed ones, perceiving through their fearless hearts the compassionate nature
of this bow-bearer, gazed at his form, their eyes attaining the full reward of wide-open looking.
Through the bamboos with wind-filled hollows, whistling and serving the function of flutes,

children.text: śuśrāva kuñjeṣu yaśaḥ svamuccairudgīyamānaṃ vanadevatābhiḥ // Ragh(K)_2.12 //
children.translated_text: he heard his own fame being sung aloud by the forest deities in the groves.
Mixed with the mist of forest waterfalls, fragrant with flowers shaken from the treetops,
the wind, pure in its conduct, attended upon him who was weary from the heat yet had no parasol.
Forest fires subsided even without rain; there was exceptional abundance of fruit and flowers;

children.text: ūnaṃ na sattveṣvadhiko babādhe tasminvanaṃ goptari gāhamāne // Ragh(K)_2.14 //
children.translated_text: the strong did not oppress the weak among creatures — while that protector roamed the forest.

children.text: sañcārapūtāni digantarāṇi kṛtvā dinānte nilayāya gantum /
children.translated_text: Having purified the quarters of the sky by his presence, when the day drew to its close,

children.text: pracakrame pallavarāgatāmrā prabhā pataṅgasya muneśca dhenuḥ // Ragh(K)_2.15 //
children.translated_text: the cow of the sage and the radiance of the sun, both coppery-red as new sprouts, set forth to return to their abode.
The guardian of the middle world followed her, who was needed for rites to gods, ancestors, and guests,

children.text: babhūva sā tena satāṃ matena śraddheva sākṣādvidhinopapannā // Ragh(K)_2.16 //
children.translated_text: and by that conduct of the virtuous, she appeared like <s>Śraddhā</s> (Faith) herself, attended upon with proper ritual.
He traveled on, beholding forests growing dark with twilight —

children.text: yayau mṛgādhyāsitaśādvalāni śyāmāyamānāni vanāni paśyan // Ragh(K)_2.17 //
children.translated_text: herds of boars emerging from muddy pools, peacocks facing their roosting trees, deer resting on green meadows.
The cow moved slowly from the effort of carrying her heavy, milk-laden udder, and the king from the weight upon his chest;
both made their way slowly along the path back to the <s>tapovana</s> (ascetic grove), each walking with a swaying gait.
His wife, her row of eyelashes languid from unblinking gaze, drank in with her eyes — as though they had been fasting —
the sight of him returning from the forest's edge, following <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s cow.
Led before by the king on the path, and met by the king's consort coming forth,

children.text: tadantare sā virarāja dhenurdinakṣapāmadhyagateva sandhyā // Ragh(K)_2.20 //
children.translated_text: the cow shone between them like the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight) situated between day and night.
The gracious queen, with auspicious rice and a ritual vessel in hand, circumambulated the milk-cow

children.text: praṇamya cānarca viśālamasyāḥ śṛṅgāntaraṃ dvāramivātmasiddheḥ // Ragh(K)_2.21 //
children.translated_text: and, bowing, worshipped the broad space between her horns as though it were the gateway to the fulfillment of her heart's desire.
Though anxious for her calf, the cow stood still and accepted the worship — and so the couple rejoiced,

children.text: bhaktyopapanneṣu hi tadvidhānāṃ prasādacihnāni puraḥphalāni // Ragh(K)_2.22 //
children.translated_text: for among those of such nature, signs of grace are the first fruits when service is offered with devotion.

children.text: guroḥ sadārasya nipīḍya pādau samāpya sāndhyaṃ ca vidhiṃ dilīpaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dilīpa</s>, having pressed the feet of his guru along with his wife, and having completed the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight) rites,

children.text: dohāvasāne punareva dogdhrīṃ bheje bhujotsannaripurniṣaṇṇām // Ragh(K)_2.23 //
children.translated_text: once more attended upon the milk-cow seated after the milking was done — he whose enemies were crushed by the strength of his arms.
Having attended upon her with offerings and lamps placed nearby, the protector, accompanied by his wife,

children.text: krameṇa suptāmanu saṃviveśa suptotthitāṃ prātaranūdatiṣṭhat // Ragh(K)_2.24 //
children.translated_text: lay down to sleep after she slept, and in the morning rose before she awoke.

children.text: itthaṃ vrataṃ pālayataḥ prajārthaṃ samaṃ mahiṣyā mahanīyakīrteḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, as the king of illustrious fame observed his vow for the sake of offspring, together with his queen,
twenty-one days passed — his, who was fit to uproot his foes.
On another day, the sage's sacrificial cow, wishing to test the devotion of her attendant,
entered a deep cavern of <s>Gaurī</s>'s lord (<s>Śiva</s>), where grass grew at the edge of a <s>Gaṅgā</s> waterfall.
She who was unapproachable even in thought by predators — so the king, his gaze drawn to the mountain's beauty, did not notice

children.text: alakṣitābhyutpatano nṛpeṇa prasahya siṃhaḥ kila tāṃ cakarṣa // Ragh(K)_2.27 //
children.translated_text: the undetected leap of a lion, who seized her by force.
Her piteous cry, prolonged by the echoes trapped in the cave,

children.text: raśmiṣvivādāya nagendradattāṃ nivartayāmāsa nṛpasya dṛṣṭim // Ragh(K)_2.28 //
children.translated_text: pulled back the king's sight as if by reins, drawing it toward the direction granted by the lord of mountains.

children.text: sa pāṭalāyāṃ gavi tasthivāṃsaṃ dhanurdharaḥ kesariṇaṃ dadarśa /
children.translated_text: The bow-bearer saw a lion standing over the tawny cow,

children.text: adhityakāyāmiva dhātumayyāṃ rodhradrumaṃ sānumataḥ praphultam // Ragh(K)_2.29 //
children.translated_text: like a <s>lodhra</s> tree in full bloom upon a plateau veined with mineral ores on a mountainside.

children.text: tato mṛgendrasya mṛgendragāmī vadhāya vadhyasya śaraṃ śaraṇyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the king, who walked like a lord of beasts and was the refuge of the distressed, seized with urgency to slay the one deserving death,
wished to draw an arrow from his quiver — he who had forcibly uprooted his enemies before.
But the left hand of that striker remained with its fingers stuck fast upon the arrow's nock,

children.text: saktāṅguliḥ sāyakapuṅkha eva citrārpitārambha ivāvatasthe // Ragh(K)_2.31 //
children.translated_text: adorned with the luster of his nails upon the peacock-feathered shaft — as if frozen mid-action in a painting.
His fury swelling from the paralysis of his arm, the king burned inwardly with his own radiance at the offender standing near yet untouchable,
like a serpent whose power has been bound by a spell.
Then the lion, holding the cow, addressed that banner of <s>Manu</s>'s lineage, worthy of noble reverence,
in a human voice — astonishing him, though himself beyond astonishment at his own supernatural powers — the lion spoke to that lion among kings:

children.text: alaṃ mahīpāla tava śrameṇa prayuktamapyastramito vṛthā syāt /
children.translated_text: "Enough, O lord of the earth, with your exertion. Even a weapon discharged from here would be in vain,

children.text: na pādaponmūlanaśakti raṃhaḥ śiloccaye mūrchati mārutasya // Ragh(K)_2.34 //
children.translated_text: for the force of the wind, though it can uproot trees, loses its power against a rocky peak."
"Know me to be <s>Kumbhodara</s>, friend of <s>Nikumbha</s>, a servant of the Eight-formed Lord (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: avaihi māṃ kiṅkaramaṣṭamūrteḥ kumbhodaraṃ nāma nikumbhamitram // Ragh(K)_2.35 //
children.translated_text: upon whose back the feet of Him who mounts the <s>Kailāsa</s>-white bull have been graciously placed."

children.text: amuṃ puraḥ paśyasi devadāruṃ putrīkṛto 'yaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajena /
children.translated_text: "Do you see that <s>devadāru</s> (divine cedar) tree before you? It was adopted as a son by the Bull-bannered One (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: yo hemakumbhastananiḥsṛtānāṃ skandasya mātuḥ payasāṃ rasajñaḥ // Ragh(K)_2.36 //
children.translated_text: who savors the milk flowing from the golden pot-like breasts of <s>Skanda</s>'s mother (<s>Pārvatī</s>)."
"Once, a wild elephant scratching its flank against it tore off its bark,
and the Daughter of the Mountain (<s>Pārvatī</s>) grieved for it as for her son <s>Senānī</s> (<s>Skanda</s>) wounded by demon weapons."
"From that time forth, I have been appointed by the Trident-bearer (<s>Śiva</s>) in this mountain cavern
to frighten away elephants, given the form of a lion with the nature of a creature dwelling in his lap."
"This cow, appointed at her destined time by the Supreme Lord, is sufficient to satisfy my hunger —

children.text: upasthitā śoṇitapāraṇā me suradviṣaścāndramasī sudheva // Ragh(K)_2.39 //
children.translated_text: my blood-feast has arrived, like the <s>sudhā</s> (nectar) of the moon for the enemies of the gods (<s>asuras</s>)."

children.text: sa tvaṃ nivartasva vihāya lajjāṃ gurorbhavāndarśitaśiṣyabhaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: "So you — turn back, abandon your shame; you have shown your pupil's devotion to your guru.

children.text: śastreṇa rakṣyaṃ yadaśakyarakṣaṃ na tadyaśaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ kṣiṇoti // Ragh(K)_2.40 //
children.translated_text: When that which is to be protected cannot be saved by weapons, it does not diminish the glory of the weapon-bearer."

children.text: iti pragalbhaṃ puruṣādhirājo mṛgādhirājasya vaco niśamya /
children.translated_text: Thus, having heard the bold speech of the lord of beasts,
the supreme lord of men, his weapons repelled by the power of <s>Giriśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), set aside his self-reproach.
And he replied to him — he whose effort had been thwarted in the earlier encounter with the arrow,
rendered immobile by the gaze of the Three-eyed One (<s>Śiva</s>), like <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> (<s>Indra</s>) wishing to hurl his thunderbolt but unable.

children.text: saṃruddhaceṣṭasya mṛgendra kāmaṃ hāsyaṃ vacastadyadahaṃ vivakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: "O lord of beasts, the words I wish to speak may well seem laughable, coming from one whose actions are paralyzed,

children.text: antargataṃ prāṇabhṛtāṃ tu veda sarvaṃ bhavānbhāvamato 'bhidhāsye // Ragh(K)_2.43 //
children.translated_text: but you know the innermost feelings of all living beings — therefore I shall speak."
"He is revered by me — the cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution of all things, moving and unmoving.
Yet this too is the wealth of my guru, consecrated to the sacred fire — perishing before my eyes, it is not to be disregarded."

children.text: sa tvaṃ madīyena śarīravṛttiṃ dehena nirvartayituṃ prasīda /
children.translated_text: "Be pleased, then, to sustain your bodily needs with my body.
Let this cow of the great sage be released — her young calf is anxious for her at the close of day."
Then, splitting the darkness of the mountain caverns with the rays of his fangs,

children.text: bhūyaḥ sa bhūteśvarapārśvavartī kiñcidvihasyārthapatiṃ babhāṣe // Ragh(K)_2.46 //
children.translated_text: that attendant of the Lord of Beings (<s>Śiva</s>), laughing slightly, spoke again to the lord of wealth:

children.text: ekātapatraṃ jagataḥ prabhutvaṃ navaṃ vayaḥ kāntamidaṃ vapuśca /
children.translated_text: "Sole sovereignty over the world beneath one parasol, the bloom of youth, and this handsome form —

children.text: alpasya hetorbahu hātumicchan vicāramugdhaḥ pratibhāsi me tvam // Ragh(K)_2.47 //
children.translated_text: you who wish to abandon much for the sake of little appear to me bewildered in your judgment."

children.text: bhūtānukampā tava cediyaṃ gaurekā bhavetsvastimatī tvadante /
children.translated_text: "If this is your compassion for living beings, then by your death this one cow alone would be safe,

children.text: jīvanpunaḥ śaśvadupaplavebhyaḥ prajāḥ prajānātha piteva pāsi // Ragh(K)_2.48 //
children.translated_text: whereas alive, you perpetually protect your subjects from calamities, O lord of people, like a father."
"Or if you fear punishment from your guru for the offense against a single cow,

children.text: śakyo 'sya manyurbhavatā vinetuṃ gāḥ koṭiśaḥ sparśayatā ghaṭodhnīḥ // Ragh(K)_2.49 //
children.translated_text: his anger can be appeased by you through the gift of millions of cows with streaming udders."
"Therefore preserve your own vigorous body, the enjoyer of an unbroken succession of auspicious things.
For they say that kingship, differing from the realm of <s>Indra</s> only by touching the earth's surface, is a rich inheritance."
When the lord of beasts had finished speaking thus, the mountain peak, through its cave-born echo,
seemed itself to repeat that very message to the king with great affection.

children.text: tathā samarthāṃ giramūcivāṃsaṃ pratyāha devānucaraṃ dilīpaḥ /
children.translated_text: To him who had spoken such cogent words, <s>Dilīpa</s> replied to the divine attendant,

children.text: dhenvā tadadhyāsanakātarākṣyā nirīkṣyamāṇaḥ sutarāṃ dayāluḥ // Ragh(K)_2.52 //
children.translated_text: all the more compassionate as he was watched by the cow with eyes trembling in fear from the lion's hold upon her:

children.text: kṣatātkila trāyata ityudagraḥ kṣattrasya śabdo bhuvaneṣu rūḍhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The exalted word <s>Kṣatra</s> (warrior) has taken root in the worlds because 'he saves from harm' —
of what use is kingship to one who acts contrary to that, or of what use is a life stained with reproach?"
"And how could the great sage's displeasure be appeased by the gift of other milk-cows?

children.text: imāmanūnāṃ surabheravaihi rudraujasā tu prahṛtaṃ tvayāsyām // Ragh(K)_2.54 //
children.translated_text: Know this one to be without equal among <s>Surabhī</s>'s offspring — yet you have assailed her with the might of <s>Rudra</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)."

children.text: seyaṃ svadehārpaṇaniṣkrayeṇa nyāyyaṃ mayā mocayituṃ bhavattaḥ /
children.translated_text: "It is right that I should ransom her from you at the price of offering my own body.

children.text: na pāraṇā syādvihatā tavaivaṃ bhavedaluptaśca muneḥ kriyārthaḥ // Ragh(K)_2.55 //
children.translated_text: Thus your feast would not be interrupted, and the sage's ritual purpose would remain unimpaired."
"You too are subject to another's will and understand this — for great indeed is your devotion to the <s>devadāru</s> tree.

children.text: sthātuṃ niyokturyadi śakyamagre vināśya rakṣyaṃ svayamakṣatena // Ragh(K)_2.56 //
children.translated_text: If it is possible to stand before one's master unscathed while the one to be protected is destroyed —"

children.text: kimapyahiṃsyastava cenmato 'haṃ yaśaḥśarīre bhava me dayāluḥ /
children.translated_text: "But if in your judgment I am not to be slain, then be merciful to me in my body of fame alone.

children.text: ekāntavidhvaṃsiṣu madvidhānāṃ piṇḍeṣvanāsthā khalu bhautikeṣu // Ragh(K)_2.57 //
children.translated_text: For those like me have no attachment to these material bodies, which are destined to perish utterly."
They say that a relationship begins with speaking first; ours was born when we two met at the edge of the forest.

children.text: tadbhūtanāthānuga nārhasi tvaṃ sambandhino me praṇayaṃ vihantum // Ragh(K)_2.58 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, O follower of the Lord of Beings, you should not destroy the affection of me, your kinsman. [Ragh(K) 2.58]
To the cow who had said 'so be it,' <s>Dilīpa</s>, his arms instantly freed from paralysis,
offered his own body to the lion, who had laid down his weapon, like a lump of flesh. [Ragh(K) 2.59]
At that moment, upon the protector of subjects who was watching the fierce descent of the lion,
a shower of flowers released from the hands of <s>Vidyādharas</s> fell from above. [Ragh(K) 2.60]
Hearing the nectar-like words 'Arise, my child,' he who had risen stood up,

children.text: dadarśa rājā jananīmiva svāṃ gāmagrataḥ prasraviṇīṃ na siṃham // Ragh(K)_2.61 //
children.translated_text: and the king saw before him the cow with milk flowing, like his own mother, but not the lion. [Ragh(K) 2.61]

children.text: taṃ vismitaṃ dhenuruvāca sādho māyāṃ mayodbhāvya parīkṣito 'si /
children.translated_text: The cow said to the astonished one: 'O virtuous one, having created an illusion, I have tested you.

children.text: ṛṣiprabhāvānmayi nāntako 'pi prabhuḥ prahartuṃ kimutānyahiṃsrāḥ // Ragh(K)_2.62 //
children.translated_text: By the power of the sage, not even <s>Antaka</s> (Death) is able to strike me — what then of other predators?' [Ragh(K) 2.62]

children.text: bhaktyā gurau mayyanukampayā ca prītāsmi te putra varaṃ vṛṇīṣva /
children.translated_text: 'By your devotion to your guru and compassion toward me, I am pleased, O son — choose a boon.

children.text: na kevalānāṃ payasāṃ prasūtimavaihi māṃ kāmadughāṃ prasannām // Ragh(K)_2.63 //
children.translated_text: Know me to be the wish-fulfilling one (<s>Kāmadhuk</s>), graciously disposed — not merely a producer of milk.' [Ragh(K) 2.63]

children.text: tataḥ samānīya sa mānitārthī hastau svahastārjitavīraśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then he, who desired a worthy end and had earned the title of hero by his own hands, joining his palms,

children.text: vaṃśasya kartāramanantakīrtiṃ sudakṣiṇāyāṃ tanayaṃ yayāce // Ragh(K)_2.64 //
children.translated_text: asked of <s>Sudakṣiṇā</s> a son who would be the perpetuator of his lineage and of endless fame. [Ragh(K) 2.64]

children.text: santānakāmāya tatheti kāmaṃ rājñe pratiśrutya payasvinī sā /
children.translated_text: Having promised 'so be it' to the king who desired offspring, that milk-cow,

children.text: dugdhvā payaḥ pattrapuṭe madīyaṃ putropayuṅkṣveti tamādideśa // Ragh(K)_2.65 //
children.translated_text: having milked her own milk into a cup of leaves, instructed him: 'Let your son partake of this.' [Ragh(K) 2.65]
'After [setting aside portions] for the calf and for the remainder of the ritual offering to the sage, O mother,

children.text: ūdhasyamicchāmi tavopabhoktuṃ ṣaṣṭhāṃśamurvyā iva rakṣitāyāḥ // Ragh(K)_2.66 //
children.translated_text: I wish to enjoy a sixth part of your udder, as of the earth that is protected.' [Ragh(K) 2.66]
Thus addressed by the lord of the earth, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s cow became exceedingly pleased,
and accompanied by him, she returned from the Himalayan valley to the hermitage without any fatigue. [Ragh(K) 2.67]

children.text: tasyāḥ prasannendumukhaḥ prasādaṃ gururnṛpāṇāṃ gurave nivedya /
children.translated_text: With a face bright as the clear moon, the preceptor of kings, having announced her grace to the guru,

children.text: mukhaprasādānumitaṃ priyāyai śaśaṃsa vācā punaruktayaiva // Ragh(K)_2.68 //
children.translated_text: told his beloved, in words that were but a repetition, what had been inferred from the brightness of his face. [Ragh(K) 2.68]
He, of blameless soul, affectionate toward the calf, having received <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s permission,

children.text: papau vasiṣṭhena kṛtābhyanujñaḥ śuddhaṃ yaśo bhūya ivāvitṛptaḥ // Ragh(K)_2.69 //
children.translated_text: drank <s>Nandinī</s>'s milk — the remainder left by the calf — like one unsated drinking pure fame again. [Ragh(K) 2.69]
Then in the morning, at the conclusion of the prescribed observance, having performed the auspicious benediction for departure,

children.text: tau dampatī svāṃ prati rājadhānīṃ prasthāpayāmāsa vaśī vasiṣṭhaḥ // Ragh(K)_2.70 //
children.translated_text: the self-controlled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> set the royal couple forth toward their own capital. [Ragh(K) 2.70]
Having circumambulated the sacrificial fire, and then <s>Arundhatī</s>, the wife of the preceptor,

children.text: dhenuṃ savatsāṃ ca nṛpaḥ pratasthe sanmaṅgalodagratarānubhāvaḥ // Ragh(K)_2.71 //
children.translated_text: and the cow with her calf, the king set out, his glory heightened by auspicious omens. [Ragh(K) 2.71]
Together with his lawful wife, that patient one traveled the road in a chariot whose sound was pleasing to the ear,

children.text: yayāvanudghātasukhena mārgaṃ sveneva pūrṇena manorathena // Ragh(K)_2.72 //
children.translated_text: smooth and free from jolts, as if on his own fulfilled desire. [Ragh(K) 2.72]

The subjects, who had been filled with longing by his absence, drank in with their eyes — which could not attain satisfaction — their lord, whose body was emaciated from the vow undertaken for the sake of progeny,
as [the herbs drink in] the newly risen lord of herbs (the moon). [Ragh(K) 2.73]
Possessing the splendor of <s>Purandara</s> (Indra), entering the city adorned with banners, acclaimed by the citizens,

children.text: bhuje bhujaṅgendrasamānasāre bhūyaḥ sa bhūmerdhuramāsasañja // Ragh(K)_2.74 //
children.translated_text: he once again took upon his arm, equal in strength to the king of serpents, the burden of the earth. [Ragh(K) 2.74]

children.text: atha nayanasamutthaṃ jyotiratreriva dyauḥ surasaridiva tejo vahniniṣṭhyūtamaiśam /
children.translated_text: Then, as the sky [conceived] the light born from the eye of <s>Atri</s>, as the celestial river [conceived] the fire discharged by <s>Agni</s> from <s>Īśa</s> (Śiva),

children.text: narapatikulabhūtyai garbhamādhatta rājñī gurubhirabhiniviṣṭaṃ lokapālānubhāvaiḥ // Ragh(K)_2.75 //
children.translated_text: so the queen conceived for the prosperity of the royal lineage an embryo infused with the powers of the <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians) who are venerable. [Ragh(K) 2.75]

body.translated_text: Thus ends the second canto of the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem).

children.translated_text: Then, when the long-awaited prosperity of her lord had arrived, its face like the moonlight for the gazing of her circle of companions,

children.text: nidānamikṣvākukulasya santateḥ sudakṣiṇā dauhadalakṣaṇaṃ dadhau // Ragh(K)_3.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sudakṣiṇā</s>, the source of the continuation of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage, bore the signs of pregnancy cravings (<s>dohada</s>). [Ragh(K) 3.1]
She, with her slender body and moderate ornaments, with a face pale as a <s>ketaka</s> petal,

children.text: sthitālpatārāṃ karuṇendumaṇḍalāṃ vibhātakalpāṃ rajanīṃ vyaḍambayat // Ragh(K)_3.2 //
children.translated_text: resembled a night near dawn — with a compassionate moon-disc having few remaining stars. [Ragh(K) 3.2]

children.text: tadānanaṃ sevitamṛttikālavaṃ nṛpaḥ samāghrāya na tṛptimāyayau /
children.translated_text: The king, having smelled that face touched with the fragrance of earth,

children.text: karīva siktaṃ pṛṣataiḥ payomucāṃ śucivyapāye vanarājipalvalam // Ragh(K)_3.3 //
children.translated_text: did not attain satisfaction — like an elephant [sniffing] a pool at the edge of a forest, sprinkled with drops from rain clouds, at the end of the hot season. [Ragh(K) 3.3]

children.text: divaṃ marutvāniva bhokṣyate mahīṃ digantaviśrāntaratho hi matsutaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'My son will enjoy the earth as <s>Marutvān</s> (Indra) [enjoys] heaven, for his chariot will rest at the ends of the quarters.'

children.text: ato 'bhilāṣe prathamaṃ tathāvidhe mano babandhānyarasānvilaṅghya sā // Ragh(K)_3.4 //
children.translated_text: Thus, she first fixed her mind on such a desire, passing over other sentiments. [Ragh(K) 3.4]

children.text: na me hriyā śaṃsati kiñcidīpsitaṃ spṛhāvatī vastuṣu keṣu māgadhī /
children.translated_text: 'She does not tell me, out of modesty, what she desires — for what objects does the princess of <s>Magadha</s> yearn?'
Thus the lord of <s>Uttarakosala</s>, excessively attentive, used to ask the companions of his beloved. [Ragh(K) 3.5]

children.text: upetya sā dohadaduḥkhaśīlatāṃ yadeva vavre tadapaśyadāhṛtam /
children.translated_text: Having attained the disposition of suffering from pregnancy cravings, whatever she wished for, she saw brought to her.
For nothing desired by her, whose bow was ever strung, was difficult to obtain even in the triple heaven. [Ragh(K) 3.6]
As the days passed, her pair of breasts, whose tips were pale as <s>madhūka</s> flowers, turning dark,
bore the beauty of a pair of caskets made of elephant tusks with lids of buffalo hide. [Ragh(K) 3.7]

children.text: krameṇa nistīrya ca dohadavyathāmupoḍhagātropacayā rarāja sā /
children.translated_text: Having gradually passed through the distress of pregnancy cravings, she, with her body having gained fullness, shone resplendent,
like a creeper that, after the shedding of old leaves, has put forth lovely new shoots. [Ragh(K) 3.8]
As the sea-girt earth conceals a treasure within, as the <s>Śamī</s> tree conceals fire hidden within,

children.text: nadīmivāntaḥsalilāṃ sarasvatīṃ nṛpaḥ sagarbhāṃ mahiṣīmamanyata // Ragh(K)_3.9 //
children.translated_text: as the river <s>Sarasvatī</s> flows with water underground — so the king regarded his pregnant queen. [Ragh(K) 3.9]
Of the love born of affection for his beloved, of the heart's elation, and of the wealth extending to the horizons won by his arms —

children.text: yathākramaṃ puṃsavanādikāḥ kriyā dhṛteśca dhīraḥ sadṛśīrvyadhatta saḥ // Ragh(K)_3.10 //
children.translated_text: that steadfast one performed in due order the rites beginning with <s>puṃsavana</s> (the ceremony for a male child), befitting his resolve and fortune. [Ragh(K) 3.10]
When she, bearing the gravity of her womb under the protection of the mother of <s>Surendra</s> (Indra), came home, released with effort from her seat,
the king delighted in her, whose eyes were tremulous and whose hands were marked from making the offering gesture (<s>añjali</s>). [Ragh(K) 3.11]
Then, when the birthing chamber was attended by skilled nurses of princes and by trusted physicians,

children.text: niratyayāya prasavāya tasthuṣī babhau samāsannaphalā kriyeva sā // Ragh(K)_3.12 //
children.translated_text: she, standing ready for a safe delivery, shone like a ritual action whose fruit is near at hand. [Ragh(K) 3.12]
Then, with five planets in exalted positions, invisible to the sun, indicating the abundance of fortune,

children.text: asūta putraṃ samaye śacīsamā trisādhanā śaktirivārthamakṣatam // Ragh(K)_3.13 //
children.translated_text: she, equal to <s>Śacī</s>, gave birth to a son at the right time, like a threefold power yielding its undiminished purpose. [Ragh(K) 3.13]
The quarters became clear, auspicious winds blew, the sacrificial fire received the oblation with its flames turning rightward;

children.text: babhūva sarvaṃ śubhaśaṃsi tatkṣaṇaṃ bhavo hi lokābhyudayāya tādṛśām // Ragh(K)_3.14 //
children.translated_text: everything at that moment was auspicious in its portents, for the birth of such beings is for the welfare of the world. [Ragh(K) 3.14]

children.text: ariṣṭaśayyāṃ parito visāriṇā sujanmanastasya nijena tejasā /
children.translated_text: By his own innate radiance, spreading all around the lying-in bed, the luster of the newly born one

children.text: niśīthadīpāḥ sahasā hatatviṣo babhūvurālekhyasamarpitā iva // Ragh(K)_3.15 //
children.translated_text: suddenly dimmed the night-lamps, as if they had been rendered into mere paintings. [Ragh(K) 3.15]
To the inner-chamber attendants who announced the prince's birth — words equal to nectar —

children.text: adeyamāsīttrayameva bhūpateḥ śaśiprabhaṃ chattramubhe ca cāmare // Ragh(K)_3.16 //
children.translated_text: there was nothing the king could not give, except only three things: the moon-bright parasol and the two flywhisks. [Ragh(K) 3.16]

children.text: sa vīkṣya putrasya cirātpitā mukhaṃ nidhānakumbhasya yuveva durgataḥ /
children.translated_text: That father, gazing long at his son's face, like a destitute man [gazing at] the opening of a treasure-pot,

children.text: mudā śarīre prababhūva nātmanaḥ payodhirindūdayamūrchito yathā // Ragh(K)_3.17 //
children.translated_text: could not contain his joy within his body, just as the ocean swells at the rising of the moon. [Ragh(K) 3.17]

children.text: sa jātakarmaṇyakhile tapasvinā tapovanādetya purodhasā kṛte /
children.translated_text: When the complete <s>jātakarma</s> (birth ceremony) had been performed by the ascetic family priest who had come from the hermitage,
<s>Dilīpa</s>'s son, like a gem extracted from a mine and given its proper setting, shone all the more. [Ragh(K) 3.18]
The sounds of auspicious instruments, pleasing to the ear, together with the joyous dancing of courtesans,

children.text: na kevalaṃ sadmani māgadhīpateḥ pathi vyajṛmbhanta divaukasāmapi // Ragh(K)_3.19 //
children.translated_text: resounded not only in the palace of the lord of <s>Magadha</s>, but also along the path of the gods (the sky). [Ragh(K) 3.19]
There was no one held in bondage whom that protector, delighted by the birth of his son, would not release.

children.text: ṛṇābhidhānātsvayameva kevalaṃ tadā pitṚṇāṃ mumuce sa bandhanāt // Ragh(K)_3.20 //
children.translated_text: Then, solely from what is called 'the debt,' he freed himself from the bondage to the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors). [Ragh(K) 3.20]

children.text: śrutasya yāyādayamantamarbhakastathā pareṣāṃ yudhi ceti pārthivaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This child will reach the end of learning, and likewise [the end] of enemies in battle' — thus the king,
discerning of meaning, considering the root <s>dhātu</s> meaning 'to go,' gave his own offspring the name <s>Raghu</s>. [Ragh(K) 3.21]

children.text: pituḥ prayatnātsa samagrasampadaḥ śubhaiḥ śarīrāvayavairdine dine /
children.translated_text: Through his father's care and the complete excellences of his auspicious bodily limbs, day by day,
he grew in increase, like the young moon through the entry of the rays of the sun whose steeds are tawny. [Ragh(K) 3.22]

children.text: umāvṛṣāṅkau śarajanmanā yathā yathā jayantena śacīpurandarau /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Umā</s> and the Bull-bannered One (<s>Vṛṣāṅka</s>, Śiva) [delighted] in <s>Skanda</s> (born of the arrow), just as <s>Śacī</s> and <s>Purandara</s> (Indra) [delighted] in <s>Jayanta</s>,

children.text: tathā nṛpaḥ sā ca sutena māgadhī nanandatustatsadṛśena tatsamau // Ragh(K)_3.23 //
children.translated_text: so the king and that princess of <s>Magadha</s>, equal to them, delighted in their son who was worthy of them. [Ragh(K) 3.23]

children.text: rathāṅganāmnoriva bhāvabandhanaṃ babhūva yatprema parasparaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: The love that existed between them toward each other — like the bond of the <s>cakravāka</s> birds —

children.text: vibhaktamapyekasute na tattayoḥ parasparasyopari paryahīyata // Ragh(K)_3.24 //
children.translated_text: though divided on account of their only son, did not diminish for one on account of the other. [Ragh(K) 3.24]

children.text: yadāha dhātryā prathamoditaṃ vaco yayau tadīyāmavalambya cāṅgulim /
children.translated_text: When he uttered his first word, prompted by his nurse, and walked holding her finger,

children.text: abhūcca namraḥ praṇipātaśikṣayā piturmudaṃ tena tatāna so 'rbhakaḥ // Ragh(K)_3.25 //
children.translated_text: and became bowed with the training in obeisance, that child extended his father's joy. [Ragh(K) 3.25]
Lifting him onto his lap, as if he were being anointed with nectar on the skin through the bodily pleasures [of touch],
the king, with eyes three-quarters closed, attained for a long time the connoisseurship of the delight of a son's touch. [Ragh(K) 3.26]
He considered that by this son of surpassing birth — a maintainer of order who would not break from steadfastness, foremost in virtuous conduct —

children.text: svamūrtibhedena guṇāgryavṛttinā patiḥ prajānāmiva sargamātmanaḥ // Ragh(K)_3.27 //
children.translated_text: he had created, as it were, his own progeny through a division of his own form, like the Lord of creatures (<s>Prajāpati</s>) [creating] the world. [Ragh(K) 3.27]
With his topknot tied and the dancing side-locks of boyhood, accompanied by ministers' sons of his own age,
he entered the ocean of literature through the proper acquisition of letters, as through the mouth of a river. [Ragh(K) 3.28]
Then, having been invested with the sacred thread (<s>upanayana</s>) according to rite, the learned preceptors instructed him, dear to his teachers,

children.text: avandhyayatnāśca babhūvuratra te kriyā hi vastūpahitā prasīdati // Ragh(K)_3.29 //
children.translated_text: and their efforts bore fruit, for indeed an action applied to a worthy object succeeds. [Ragh(K) 3.29]
He, of noble intellect, with complete qualities, gradually mastered the four <s>vidyās</s> (branches of knowledge), comparable to the four oceans,
like the lord of tawny horses (the sun) [traversing] the quarters with winds that rush ahead. [Ragh(K) 3.30]

children.text: tvacaṃ sa medhyāṃ paridhāya rauravīmaśikṣatāstraṃ pitureva mantravat /
children.translated_text: Wearing the sacred skin of a <s>ruru</s> deer, he learned the science of weapons from his father alone, along with their <s>mantras</s>,

children.text: prayogasaṃhārarahasyavittamo babhūva cāstreṣu yathā purandaraḥ // Ragh(K)_3.31//
children.translated_text: and became the foremost knower of the secrets of their deployment, withdrawal, and mysteries, like <s>Purandara</s> (Indra) himself among weapons. [Ragh(K) 3.31]

children.text: mahokṣatāṃ vatsataraḥ spṛśanniva dvipendrabhāvaṃ kalabhaḥ śrayanniva /
children.translated_text: Like a young bull approaching the state of a great ox, like a young elephant assuming the majesty of a lordly elephant,

children.text: raghuḥ kramādyauvanabhinnaśaiśavaḥ pupoṣa gambhīramanoharaṃ vapuḥ // Ragh(K)_3.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Raghu</s>, gradually breaking through childhood into youth, nourished a form that was deep and captivating. [Ragh(K) 3.32]
Then, after the <s>godāna</s> ceremony (the rite of shaving), the lord arranged the consecration for his marriage.

children.text: narendrakanyāstamavāpya satpatiṃ tamopahaṃ dakṣasutā ivābabhuḥ // Ragh(K)_3.33 //
children.translated_text: The princesses, having obtained him as a worthy husband, became like the daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s> who obtained the destroyer of darkness. [Ragh(K) 3.33]
A youth, with long arms extended like a yoke, broad-shouldered, with a chest like a door-panel, and a well-developed neck,
<s>Raghu</s>, though surpassing his father in bodily excellence, yet appeared small through his humility. [Ragh(K) 3.34]

children.text: atha prajānāṃ ciramātmanā dhṛtāṃ nitāntagurvīṃ laghayiṣyatā dhuram /
children.translated_text: Then, wishing to lighten the exceedingly heavy burden of governance that he had long borne himself over the subjects,

children.text: vaśīti matvā maticakṣuṣā suto nṛpeṇa cakre yuvarājaśabdabhāk // Ragh(K)_3.35 //
children.translated_text: the king, perceiving with the eye of wisdom that his son was self-controlled, made him bear the title of <s>Yuvarāja</s> (crown prince). [Ragh(K) 3.35]
After the abode rooted in the king, <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune), who delights in virtues, went to that seat designated as <s>Yuvarāja</s>,
in partial measure, as from a lotus to a newly blooming water-lily. [Ragh(K) 3.36]
Like the dawn with the wind as its charioteer, like the radiant sun at the dispersal of clouds,

children.text: babhūva tenātitarāṃ durutsahaḥ kaṭaprabhedena karīva pārthivaḥ // Ragh(K)_3.37 //
children.translated_text: the king became exceedingly formidable through him, like an elephant at the splitting of its temples. [Ragh(K) 3.37]
Appointing him to the guarding of the sacrificial horse, followed by princes bearing bows,

children.text: apūrṇamekena śatakratūpamaḥ śataṃ kratūnāmapavighnamāpa saḥ // Ragh(K)_3.38 //
children.translated_text: he, equal to the performer of a hundred sacrifices (<s>Indra</s>), completed, lacking but one, a hundred sacrifices without obstruction. [Ragh(K) 3.38]

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ tena makhāya yajvanā turaṅgamutsṛṣṭamanargalaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thereafter, the horse released by that sacrificer for the sacrifice, roaming unrestricted,

children.text: dhanurbhṛtāmagrata eva rakṣiṇāṃ jahāra śakraḥ kila gūḍhavigrahaḥ // Ragh(K)_3.39 //
children.translated_text: was stolen by <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) himself, they say, who had concealed his form, right before the armed guardians. [Ragh(K) 3.39]

children.text: viṣādaluptapratipatti vismitaṃ kumārasainyaṃ sapadi sthitaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: That army of the prince, bewildered, its resolve destroyed by dismay, stood still;

children.text: vasiṣṭhadhenuśca yadṛcchayāgatā śrutaprabhāvā dadṛśe 'tha nandinī // Ragh(K)_3.40 //
children.translated_text: and then <s>Nandinī</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s cow, of renowned power, appeared there, having come of her own accord. [Ragh(K) 3.40]

children.text: tadaṅganiḥṣyandalavena locane pramṛjya puṇyena puraskṛtaḥ satām /
children.translated_text: Having wiped his eyes with her sacred tears streaming from her body, honored by the virtuous,
<s>Dilīpa</s>'s son (<s>Raghu</s>) gained the ability to perceive even supersensory realities. [Ragh(K) 3.41]

children.text: sa pūrvataḥ parvatapakṣaśātanaṃ dadarśa devaṃ naradevasambhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, born of a king among men, saw to the east the god who was the clipper of the wings of mountains,

children.text: punaḥ punaḥ sūtaniṣiddhacāpalaṃ harantamaśvaṃ ratharaśmisaṃyutam // Ragh(K)_3.42 //
children.translated_text: leading away the horse yoked to a chariot, its restlessness repeatedly checked by the charioteer. [Ragh(K) 3.42]
Recognizing him to be <s>Hari</s> (Indra) by his thousand unblinking eyes and by his tawny horses,

children.text: avocadenaṃ gaganaspṛśā raghuḥ svareṇa dhīreṇa nivartayanniva // Ragh(K)_3.43 //
children.translated_text: <s>Raghu</s> addressed him with a voice touching the sky, deep-toned, as if making him turn back: [Ragh(K) 3.43]

children.text: makhāṃśabhājāṃ prathamo manīṣibhistvameva devendra yadā nigadyase /
children.translated_text: 'You who are declared by the wise to be the foremost among those who partake of sacrificial shares, O Lord of Gods (<s>Devendra</s>) —'

children.text: ajasradīkṣāprayatasya madguroḥ kriyāvighātāya kathaṃ pravartase // Ragh(K)_3.44 //
children.translated_text: How do you proceed to obstruct the rites of my guru, who is exerting himself in perpetual consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>)? [Ragh(K) 3.44]

children.text: trilokanāthena satā makhadviṣastvayā niyāmyā nanu divyacakṣuṣā /
children.translated_text: You, the lord of the three worlds, possessed of the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>), should indeed restrain the enemies of sacrifice (<s>makhadviṣ</s>);

children.text: sa cetsvayaṃ karmasu dharmacāriṇāṃ tvamantarāyībhavasi cyuto vidhiḥ // Ragh(K)_3.45 //
children.translated_text: but if you yourself become an obstacle to the rites of those who follow <s>dharma</s>, then the divine order has fallen. [Ragh(K) 3.45]
Therefore, O <s>Maghavan</s>, you should release this horse, the foremost limb of the great sacrifice;

children.text: pathaḥ śucerdarśayitāra īśvarā malīmasāmādadate na paddhatim // Ragh(K)_3.46 //
children.translated_text: lords show the pure path — they do not adopt the way of the tainted. [Ragh(K) 3.46]

children.text: iti pragalbhaṃ raghuṇā samīritaṃ vaco niśamyādhipatirdivaukasām /
children.translated_text: Having heard those bold words spoken by <s>Raghu</s>, the lord of the celestials

children.text: nivartayāmāsa rathaṃ savismayaḥ pracakrame ca prativaktumuttaram // Ragh(K)_3.47 //
children.translated_text: turned his chariot around with astonishment, and began to speak a reply: [Ragh(K) 3.47]

children.text: yathāttha rājanyakumāra tattathā yaśastu rakṣyaṃ parito yaśodhanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "What you say, O prince of the warrior class, is true; but fame must be guarded on all sides by those whose wealth is fame.
Your guru is intent on surpassing, through sacrifice, all of that world-illuminating [fame] of mine. [Ragh(K) 3.48]

children.text: hariryathaikaḥ puruṣottamaḥ smṛto maheśvarastryambaka eva nāparaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Hari</s> alone is renowned as the supreme being (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), and <s>Maheśvara</s> is the three-eyed one (<s>Tryambaka</s>) and no other,

children.text: tathā vidurmāṃ munayaḥ śatakratuṃ dvitīyagāmī na hi śabda eṣa naḥ // Ragh(K)_3.49 //
children.translated_text: so the sages know me as the one of a hundred sacrifices (<s>Śatakratu</s>) — this epithet of ours does not admit a second claimant. [Ragh(K) 3.49]
Therefore this horse has been taken by me, who imitated <s>Kapila</s>, from the [sacrifice of] your father.

children.text: alaṃ prayatnena tavātra mā nidhāḥ padaṃ padavyāṃ sagarasya santateḥ // Ragh(K)_3.50 //
children.translated_text: Enough of your effort in this matter! Do not set foot on the path of <s>Sagara</s>'s lineage!" [Ragh(K) 3.50]
Then, laughing, the son of the earth-lord (<s>Indra</s> among kings) spoke again to <s>Purandara</s>, with fear dispelled:

children.text: gṛhāṇa śastraṃ yadi sarga eṣa te na khalvanirjitya raghuṃ kṛtī bhavān // Ragh(K)_3.51 //
children.translated_text: "Take up your weapon if this is your resolve — for surely you cannot be victorious without defeating <s>Raghu</s>." [Ragh(K) 3.51]

children.text: sa evamuktvā maghavantamunmukhaḥ kariṣyamāṇaḥ saśaraṃ śarāsanam /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Maghavan</s>, he stood facing him, ready to act, bow in hand with arrow fitted,
resplendent with the excellence of his body in the <s>ālīḍha</s> (archer's) stance, rivaling <s>Śiva</s> himself. [Ragh(K) 3.52]
<s>Raghu</s>'s arrow, full of defiant resolve, struck the heart of even the wrathful mountain-splitter (<s>Indra</s>);
upon his bow, marked for a moment like fresh rain-clouds, he fitted an unerring shaft. [Ragh(K) 3.53]
That arrow, accustomed to the blood of terrible <s>Asuras</s>, penetrated the broad chest of the prince
and, as if with curiosity, tasted human blood for the first time. [Ragh(K) 3.54]
The son of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Indra</s>), though of valor equal to <s>Kumāra</s> (<s>Skanda</s>), on his arm — its fingers hardened by striking the celestial elephant —

children.text: bhuje śacīpattraviśeṣakāṅkite svanāmacihnaṃ nicakhāna sāyakam // Ragh(K)_3.55 //
children.translated_text: marked with the ornamental pattern of <s>Śacī</s>, engraved an arrow bearing the mark of his own name. [Ragh(K) 3.55]

children.text: jahāra cānyena mayūralāñchanaṃ śareṇa śakrasya mahāśanidhvajam /
children.translated_text: And with another arrow, he knocked down the peacock-emblazoned banner of <s>Śakra</s>, bearing the great thunderbolt standard;

children.text: cukopa tasmai sa bhṛśaṃ suraśriyaḥ prasahya keśavyaparopaṇādiva // Ragh(K)_3.56 //
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> was greatly enraged at him, as if by the forcible tearing away of the glory of the gods. [Ragh(K) 3.56]
Between those two, with their armies of <s>Siddhas</s> standing nearby, with arrows terrifying to behold like <s>Garutmat</s> (eagles) and serpents,

children.text: babhūva yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ jayaiṣiṇoradhomukhairūrdhvamukhaiśca pattribhiḥ // Ragh(K)_3.57 //
children.translated_text: there arose a tumultuous battle, both seeking victory, with shafts flying downward and upward. [Ragh(K) 3.57]
With the continuous volleys of weapons discharged in rapid succession, <s>Vāsava</s> could not extinguish

children.text: śaśāka nirvāpayituṃ na vāsavaḥ svataścyutaṃ vahnimivādbhirambudaḥ // Ragh(K)_3.58 //
children.translated_text: that repository of irresistible splendor — like a rain-cloud [unable to extinguish] with its waters a fire that has fallen from itself. [Ragh(K) 3.58]
Then from his forearm, marked with <s>Hari</s>-sandal paste, <s>Raghu</s>, with an arrow whose tip was [shaped like] a half-moon,
severed the bowstring of <s>Indra</s>, which roared with the sound of a churned ocean. [Ragh(K) 3.59]

children.text: sa cāpamutsṛjya vivṛddhamatsaraḥ pravāsanāya prabalasya vidviṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, releasing his bow, his fury increased, [seeking] to banish the mighty foe,
seized a weapon with a blazing halo of radiance, [terrible] like the uprooting of mountain wings. [Ragh(K) 3.60]

children.text: raghurbhṛśaṃ vakṣasi tena tāḍitaḥ papāta bhūmau saha sainikāsrubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Raghu</s>, struck severely on the chest by that [weapon], fell to the earth, along with the tears of his soldiers;

children.text: nimeṣamātrādavadhūya ca vyathāṃ sahotthitaḥ sainikaharṣaniḥsvanaiḥ // Ragh(K)_3.61 //
children.translated_text: but shaking off the pain in the blink of an eye, he rose up again amidst the joyful shouts of his army. [Ragh(K) 3.61]
Even so, as he stood firm in his adversarial stance, cruel in the practice of weapons,

children.text: tutoṣa vīryātiśayena vṛtrahā padaṃ hi sarvatra guṇairvidhīyate // Ragh(K)_3.62 //
children.translated_text: the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> was pleased by his surpassing valor — for distinction is achieved everywhere through qualities. [Ragh(K) 3.62]

children.text: asaṅgamadriṣvapi sāravattayā na me tvadanyena visoḍhamāyudham /
children.translated_text: "My weapon, irresistible even against mountains, has been endured by none other than you.

children.text: avaihi māṃ prītamṛte turaṅgamādvaraṃ vṛṇīṣveti tamāha vṛtrahā // Ragh(K)_3.63 //
children.translated_text: Know me to be pleased — choose a boon other than the horse" — thus spoke the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> to him. [Ragh(K) 3.63]
Then the son of <s>Dilīpa</s>, withdrawing the partially drawn arrow from his quiver, his fingers tinted by the luster of its golden feathered shaft,

children.text: dilīpasūnuḥ pratisaṃharanniṣuṃ priyaṃ vadaḥ pratyavadatsureśvaram // Ragh(K)_3.64 //
children.translated_text: spoke sweet words in reply to the lord of the gods: [Ragh(K) 3.64]

children.text: amocyamaśvaṃ yadi manyate prabhustataḥ samāpte vidhineva karmaṇi /
children.translated_text: "If the lord considers the horse not to be released, then as if the rite were completed,

children.text: ajasradīkṣātanuradya me guruḥ kratoraśeṣeṇa phalena yujyatām // Ragh(K)_3.65 //
children.translated_text: let my guru, whose body is emaciated by perpetual consecration, be endowed today with the fruit of the remainder of the sacrifice. [Ragh(K) 3.65]
And as for this account — may the lord of the earth, who is unapproachable as a partial incarnation of the three-eyed one (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: tavaiva sandeśaharādviśāṃpatiḥ śṛṇoti nākeśa tathā vidhīyatām // Ragh(K)_3.66 //
children.translated_text: hear it from your own messenger when gathered in the assembly — O lord of heaven, let it be so arranged." [Ragh(K) 3.66]
Saying 'So be it,' willingly assenting to <s>Raghu</s>, <s>Mātali</s> the charioteer departed as he had come;

children.text: nṛpasya nātipramanāḥ sadogṛhaṃ sudakṣiṇāsūnurapi nyavartata // Ragh(K)_3.67 //
children.translated_text: and the king's son, not excessively elated, though he was the offspring of one skilled in generous giving, also returned to the sacrificial hall. [Ragh(K) 3.67]
The lord of creatures, informed first by <s>Hari</s>'s (<s>Indra</s>'s) command-bearer, congratulated him,
touching with a hand trembling with joy that limb of his marked with the scar of the thunderbolt. [Ragh(K) 3.68]

children.text: iti kṣitīśo navatiṃ navādhikāṃ mahākratūnāṃ mahanīyaśāsanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus the lord of the earth, of venerable command, having completed ninety-nine great sacrifices,
at the end of his lifespan, desiring to ascend to heaven, extended what seemed a series of stairways. [Ragh(K) 3.69]

children.text: atha sa viṣayavyāvṛttātmā yathāvidhi sūnave nṛpatikakudaṃ dattvā yūne sitātapavāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Then he, his mind withdrawn from sense objects, having duly bestowed upon his young son the royal parasol, the white sunshade — the crest-jewel of kingship,

children.text: munivanatarucchāyāṃ devyā tayā saha śiśriye galitavayasāmikṣvākūṇāmidaṃ hi kulavratam // Ragh(K)_3.70 //
children.translated_text: along with his queen, he resorted to the shade of the trees in the hermitage grove — for this is the family vow of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> whose age has declined. [Ragh(K) 3.70]

body.translated_text: Thus ends the third canto in the great poem <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s>.

children.text: sa rājyaṃ guruṇā dattaṃ pratipadyādhikaṃ babhau /
children.translated_text: Having received the kingdom given by his elder, he shone forth even more,

children.text: dinānte nihitaṃ tejaḥ savitreva hutāśanaḥ // Ragh(K)_4.1 //
children.translated_text: like the sacrificial fire [receiving] the radiance deposited [in it] by the sun at the end of the day. [Ragh(K) 4.1]

children.text: nyastaśastraṃ dilīpaṃ ca taṃ ca śuśruvuṣāṃ prabhum /
children.translated_text: That <s>Dilīpa</s> had laid down his arms, and that this one was their [new] lord eager to be obeyed —
for kings whose arrow-heads had been removed, this was like a spear planted in the heart. [Ragh(K) 4.2]
Like those [celebrating] the banner of <s>Puruhūta</s> (<s>Indra</s>), the rows of his festive installations,
heralding new prosperity, delighted the subjects along with their offspring. [Ragh(K) 4.3]
Both were simultaneously conquered by him of the elephant's gait —
the ancestral throne and the entire circle of enemies. [Ragh(K) 4.4]
By the mark of [its] circle of shade, <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), herself invisible, they say,
with a lotus parasol, attended upon him who was consecrated for imperial sovereignty. [Ragh(K) 4.5]
<s>Sarasvatī</s> (the goddess of speech), arranging her proximity at the proper times for the panegyrists,
attended upon him who was worthy of praise, with praises that were meaningful. [Ragh(K) 4.6]
Though the earth had been enjoyed by venerable kings from <s>Manu</s> onwards,
nevertheless, under him she was as if she had never before had another [lord]. [Ragh(K) 4.7]

children.text: sa hi sarvasya lokasya yuktadaṇḍatayā manaḥ /
children.translated_text: For he, through the just application of punishment (<s>daṇḍa</s>), captivated the minds of all people,
like the gentle southern breeze, neither too cold nor too hot. [Ragh(K) 4.8]
Though his eyes were indeed like lotus petals in beauty,
his true vision came from the <s>śāstra</s> (science of polity), which discerns subtle objectives. [Ragh(K) 4.9]
Just as the moon [is named] from its delighting, and the sun from its burning heat,
so too that king was true to his name (<s>anvartha</s>), through his gladdening of the subjects. [Ragh(K) 4.10]
When the good and bad [policies] were pointed out to the new king by those versed in statecraft,
only the former existed in him — the latter had no place. [Ragh(K) 4.11]
The subjects were made only mildly nostalgic for their elder [king] by the superiority of [the new king's] virtues,

children.text: phalena sahakārasya puṣpodgama iva prajāḥ // Ragh(K)_4.12 //
children.translated_text: like the blossoming of the mango [inducing only mild longing] because of [the promise of] fruit. [Ragh(K) 4.12]
The qualities of all five elements flourished in excellence
under that new sovereign — everything seemed renewed. [Ragh(K) 4.13]
Then, the royal fortune (<s>pārthivaśrī</s>), peaceful and restored to health, approached him,
like a second autumn (<s>śarat</s>), bearing the mark of lotuses. [Ragh(K) 4.14]
The regions of the sky, lightened by the clouds that had shed their rain, of both the sun and of him,

children.text: vardhiṣṇavo diśāṃ bhāgāḥ pratāpāyeva recitāḥ // Ragh(K)_4.15 //
children.translated_text: the expanding quarters seemed cleared for the increase of glory. [Ragh(K) 4.15]
'This is the season for <s>Raghu</s> to string his weapon' — as if fearful of this,

children.text: svaṃ dhanuḥ śaṅkiteneva saṃjahre śatamanyunā // Ragh(K)_4.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śatamanya</s> (<s>Indra</s>) drew in his own bow [i.e., the rainbow]. [Ragh(K) 4.16]
Autumn imitated him with its lotuses as parasols and its blooming <s>kāśa</s>-grass as fly-whisks,

children.text: ṛturviḍambayāmāsa na punaḥ prāpa tacchriyam // Ragh(K)_4.17 //
children.translated_text: but did not attain his splendor. [Ragh(K) 4.17]
When both he, gracious of countenance, and the moon, of clear radiance,
[were present], the delight of those with eyes was equally intense for both. [Ragh(K) 4.18]
In the rows of swans, in the stars, in the night-lotuses, and in the waters,
his glories were spread about, as if they were extensions of his fame. [Ragh(K) 4.19]
The women guarding the rice fields, seated in the shade of sugarcane, sang the fame of that protector,
the rise of whose virtues was the opening theme of stories told even to children. [Ragh(K) 4.20]
The waters became clear from the rising of that one of great might born of the pot (<s>Kumbhayoni</s> = <s>Agastya</s>, i.e., the star <s>Canopus</s>);
but the minds of <s>Raghu</s>'s enemies, apprehensive of being overpowered, were disturbed. [Ragh(K) 4.21]
Great bulls, their humps raised in rut, breaking the banks of rivers,
playfully frolicking, matched the prowess of that [king]. [Ragh(K) 4.22]
Struck by the rut-scented blossoms of the seven-leaved tree (<s>saptaparṇa</s>),
his elephants, as if from jealousy, discharged their <s>mada</s>-fluid from seven openings. [Ragh(K) 4.23]
Making the rivers fordable and the roads free of sticky mud,

children.text: yātrāyai codayāmāsa taṃ śakteḥ prathamaṃ śarat // Ragh(K)_4.24 //
children.translated_text: autumn (<s>śarat</s>) first urged him to march, [the season being] the [right time for] the exercise of power. [Ragh(K) 4.24]
For him, the fire (<s>Agni</s>), duly offered to in the rite of consecrating the horses,
with its clockwise-circling flames, seemed to give him victory as if with a hand. [Ragh(K) 4.25]
He, with his base and border provinces well-guarded, his rear secure and accompanied [by allies],
taking along the sixfold army, set forth with the desire to conquer the directions. [Ragh(K) 4.26]
The city-women, elder in age, showered him with parched rice,
like the milk-ocean [showering] <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) with drops splashed up from [Mount] <s>Mandara</s>. [Ragh(K) 4.27]

children.text: sa yayau prathamaṃ prācīṃ tulyaḥ prācīnabarhiṣā /
children.translated_text: He marched first to the east, equal to <s>Prācīnabarhi</s>,
as if threatening the enemies with his banners fluttering in the wind. [Ragh(K) 4.28]
With dust raised by the chariots and elephants resembling dense clouds,
making the surface of the earth seem like the sky and the sky seem like the earth. [Ragh(K) 4.29]
His glory went first, then his fame, then the vanguard soldiers,

children.text: yayau paścādgajānīkaṃ catuḥskandheva sā camūḥ // Ragh(K)_4.30 //
children.translated_text: and behind them the elephant-army — that army marched like [one having] four divisions. [Ragh(K) 4.30]
The streams along the road were muddied by his vanguard, diminished by those marching alongside,
and turned to mud by those marching behind. [Ragh(K) 4.31]
Desert tracts he made watered, navigable rivers easily fordable,
and dense forests open — by the power of his might. [Ragh(K) 4.32]
Drawing his great army toward the eastern ocean,
he appeared like <s>Bhagīratha</s> [drawing] the <s>Gaṅgā</s> that had fallen from <s>Hara</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) matted locks. [Ragh(K) 4.33]
By kings who abandoned [their thrones], were uprooted, and were broken in many ways,
his path was strewn — like [the path] of elephants with trees. [Ragh(K) 4.34]
Thus conquering one after another the eastern territories, the victorious one
reached the vicinity of the great ocean, dark with groves of palmyra palms. [Ragh(K) 4.35]
From that lord — as if from the ocean-tide — from whom the unbowed would be uprooted,
the <s>Suhmas</s> preserved themselves by adopting the livelihood of [weaving] reeds. [Ragh(K) 4.36]
Having swiftly uprooted the <s>Vaṅgas</s>, the leader, flushed with the spoils of naval warfare,
erected victory pillars in the channels of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>'s streams. [Ragh(K) 4.37]
They, bowing at his feet like rice-plants, [though] uprooted and replanted,
nourished <s>Raghu</s> with their fruits (tribute). [Ragh(K) 4.38]
Having crossed the <s>Kāverī</s> river with his armies, using elephants as bridges,
guided by the <s>Utkalas</s>, he marched toward <s>Kaliṅga</s>. [Ragh(K) 4.39]

children.text: sa pratāpaṃ mahendrasya mūrdhni tīkṣṇaṃ nyaveśayat /
children.translated_text: He placed his fiery valor sharply upon the head of <s>Mahendra</s> (the mountain / the <s>Kaliṅga</s> king),
like a driver [placing] a goad upon an elephant that understands the deep [command]. [Ragh(K) 4.40]
The <s>Kaliṅga</s> [king], whose means were elephants, received him with weapons,
like a mountain [showering] <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — who was intent on clipping its wings — with a rain of rocks. [Ragh(K) 4.41]
The descendant of <s>Kākutstha</s>, enduring there the storm of iron arrows from the enemies,
attained the fortune of victory as if bathed in an auspicious ablution. [Ragh(K) 4.42]
From the elephant-army — dispersed by the <s>Vāyavya</s> (wind) weapon, like a wing-clipped ocean of the sky —
he seized the <s>Kaliṅga</s> [king], like <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) seizing a serpent. [Ragh(K) 4.43]
With the leaves of betel-plants, his soldiers fashioned drinking grounds,

children.text: nārikelāsavaṃ yodhāḥ śātravaṃ ca yaśaḥ papuḥ // Ragh(K)_4.44 //
children.translated_text: and drank the coconut wine and the enemy's fame alike. [Ragh(K) 4.44]
That king, a conqueror through <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmavijayī</s>), [who] captured and released [the defeated],

children.text: hriyaṃ mahendranāthasya jahāra na tu medinīm // Ragh(K)_4.45 //
