children.translated_text: took away the pride of the lord of <s>Mahendra</s>, but not his territory. [Ragh(K) 4.45]
Then, along the coastal shore itself, garlanded with fruitful areca palms,
he whose victory needed no [further] wishing marched toward the southern direction, hallowed by <s>Agastya</s>. [Ragh(K) 4.46]
He, fragrant with the rut-fluid of elephants [used for] the enjoyment of his army,
made the <s>Kāverī</s> seem suspect, as it were, to the lord of rivers (the ocean). // Ragh(K)_4.47 //
Of the <s>Kerala</s> women who had abandoned their ornaments in fear,
the dust of his army served as a substitute for cosmetic powder in their hair. // Ragh(K)_4.48 //
The foothills of <s>Malaya</s> mountain were occupied by the forces of that conqueror who had traversed the road,
their pepper plants already stripped by parrots. // Ragh(K)_4.49 //
The dust arising from the cardamom fields, whose crops were crushed by the hooves of his thoroughbred horses,

children.text: vyānaśe sapadi vyoma kīṭakośābilaṃ rajaḥ // Ragh(K)_4.50 //
children.translated_text: instantly pervaded the sky, riddled like a cocoon of silkworms. // Ragh(K)_4.50 //
The garlands offered to the sandal trees along paths where serpents coil around them
did not slip from the neck-chains of his elephants, even those that could snap the three-fold fetters. // Ragh(K)_4.51 //
In the southern quarter, even the sun's splendor grows faint;

children.text: tasyāmeva raghoḥ pāṇḍyāḥ pratāpaṃ na viṣehire // Ragh(K)_4.52 //
children.translated_text: in that very quarter, the <s>Pāṇḍyas</s> could not endure the might of <s>Raghu</s>. // Ragh(K)_4.52 //
The pearls, the essence of the great ocean where the <s>Tāmraparṇī</s> joins it,

children.text: te nipatya dadustasmai yaśaḥ svamiva sañcitam // Ragh(K)_4.53 //
children.translated_text: they prostrated and gave to him, as though it were their own accumulated fame. // Ragh(K)_4.53 //
Having enjoyed at will the two mountains <s>Malaya</s> and <s>Durdura</s>, whose slopes were rich with sandal trees,
which were like the two breasts of that (southern) quarter, // Ragh(K)_4.54 //
he of irresistible valor crossed the <s>Sahya</s> mountain, far-flung from the ocean,
which was like the hip of the earth with its garment slipping down. // Ragh(K)_4.55 //
As his armies spread forth, eager for the conquest of <s>Aparānta</s> (the western coast),
the ocean seemed as though driven back by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows, clinging to the <s>Sahya</s> range. // Ragh(K)_4.56 //
The <s>Kaitaka</s> (silk-cotton) dust blown ahead by the wind
served as an effortless silk covering for the wardrobes of his warriors. // Ragh(K)_4.57 //
The rustling sound of wind-tossed silver palm groves was drowned out
by the jingling of his horses' trappings and chariots. // Ragh(K)_4.58 //
From the <s>Punnāga</s> trees, bees fell

children.text: kaṭeṣu kariṇāṃ petuḥ punnāgebhyaḥ śilīmukhāḥ // Ragh(K)_4.59 //
children.translated_text: upon the fragrant temples of his elephants, whose neck-ropes were bound to date-palm trunks and whose rut-fluid was sweet-smelling. // Ragh(K)_4.59 //
The ocean, it is said, when entreated by <s>Rāma</s> long ago, gave passage;
now, under the pretext of the <s>Aparānta</s> kings, it paid tribute to <s>Raghu</s>. // Ragh(K)_4.60 //
The <s>Trikūṭa</s> mountain itself, bearing clear marks of valor scored by the tusks of great elephants,
he made his lofty pillar of victory there. // Ragh(K)_4.61 //
Then he set forth by the land route to conquer the <s>Pārasīkas</s> (Persians),
like a self-controlled man subduing the enemies called the senses through knowledge of truth. // Ragh(K)_4.62 //
He did not tolerate the intoxicating pride of the <s>Yavana</s> women's lotus-faces,
just as an untimely mass of clouds cannot endure the morning sunlight falling on lotuses. // Ragh(K)_4.63 //
A tumultuous battle took place between him and the <s>Pārasīka</s> horsemen,
so thick with dust that the opposing warriors could be identified only by the twanging of their <s>Śārṅga</s> bows. // Ragh(K)_4.64 //
With their bearded heads severed by broad-bladed arrows, he strewed the earth
as though covering it with sheets of honeycomb swarming with bees. // Ragh(K)_4.65 //
The survivors, having removed their helmets, went to him for refuge;
for the anger of great souls is countered by prostration. // Ragh(K)_4.66 //
His warriors then relieved the fatigue of victory with wine
in the grape-vine regions spread with precious animal skins. // Ragh(K)_4.67 //
Then <s>Raghu</s> set forth toward the northern quarter of <s>Kubera</s>, like the radiant sun,
as if to extract the essences of the northern peoples with his sharp-rayed arrows. // Ragh(K)_4.68 //
Unconquerable, having made those already-conquered kings the vanguard of his chariot forces,
he entered the northern road like the submarine fire entering the great ocean. // Ragh(K)_4.69 //
His horses, their travel-weariness relieved by rolling on the banks of the <s>Vaṅkṣu</s> (Oxus) river,
shook their shoulders to which saffron pollen still clung. // Ragh(K)_4.70 //
There, upon the women of the <s>Hūṇa</s> harems, whose husbands had displayed their valor,
<s>Raghu</s>'s deeds became evident through the scratching of their cheeks (in grief). // Ragh(K)_4.71 //
The <s>Kāmbojas</s>, unable to endure his prowess in battle,
bowed down along with their walnut trees, scarred by elephant-tethering. // Ragh(K)_4.72 //
Their towering heaps of wealth, consisting chiefly of fine horses,
flowed into that lord of men like rivers into the ocean. // Ragh(K)_4.73 //
Then, with his army, he ascended the mountain sacred to <s>Gaurī</s>'s lord (<s>Himālaya</s>),
as if augmenting its peaks with the uplifted dust of mineral ores. // Ragh(K)_4.74 //
He praised the unperturbed backward glance of the lions dwelling in caves,
who remained unalarmed even amid the clamor of his army, recognizing them as equals in valor. // Ragh(K)_4.75 //
The winds that bore the spray of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> attended him along the way,
rustling through birch trees and producing sounds in the bamboos. // Ragh(K)_4.76 //
His soldiers rested in the shadows of <s>Devadāru</s> pines, sitting upon
stone slabs whose surfaces were perfumed by the musk-deer that had sat upon them. // Ragh(K)_4.77 //
The <s>Saralā</s> (pine) trees, their splendor enhanced by the neck-ornaments of elephants rubbing against their trunks,
served as lampless lamps at night, the luminous herbs being near at hand. // Ragh(K)_4.78 //
At his encampments, the <s>Devadāru</s> trees revealed to the <s>Kirātas</s>
the stature of his elephants through the rut-moist scratch marks on their trunks. // Ragh(K)_4.79 //
There a clash occurred between <s>Raghu</s> and the mountain warriors,
in which fire sprang from the friction of stones hurled against iron arrows. // Ragh(K)_4.80 //
Having made those who would cast arrows pay tribute as a sign of festive submission, the skillful one
made the <s>Kinnaras</s> sing a victory-proclamation for his arms. // Ragh(K)_4.81 //
When they stood with offering-gifts in hand, each recognized the other's worth:

children.text: rājñā himavataḥ sāro rājñaḥ sāro himādriṇā // Ragh(K)_4.82 //
children.translated_text: the king learned the essence of <s>Himavat</s>, and <s>Himavat</s> learned the essence of the king. // Ragh(K)_4.82 //
Having established there an unshakable mass of glory, he descended,
as if taking away the pride of the mountain that had been weighed against <s>Paulastya</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>). // Ragh(K)_4.83 //
When he crossed the <s>Lauhitya</s> (Brahmaputra) river, the lord of <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s> trembled,
along with his <s>Kālāguru</s> (dark aloe) trees that had been made into elephant-tethering posts. // Ragh(K)_4.84 //
He could not endure even the dust from <s>Raghu</s>'s chariot-train, which obscured the sun without clouds and brought a false storm;
how then could he withstand his bannered army? // Ragh(K)_4.85 //
The lord of <s>Kāmarūpa</s>, recognizing his valor to exceed even <s>Indra</s>'s,
served him with those very split-templed elephants with which he had besieged others. // Ragh(K)_4.86 //
The lord of <s>Kāmarūpa</s> worshipped the shadow of his feet, the presiding deity upon a golden throne,
with offerings of jewel-flowers. // Ragh(K)_4.87 //
Thus, having conquered all the quarters, the victorious one turned back, letting settle the dust raised by his chariots
upon the heads of kings now bereft of their royal parasols. // Ragh(K)_4.88 //
He performed the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice with all his possessions as the sacrificial fee;

children.text: ādānaṃ hi visargāya satāṃ vārimucāmiva // Ragh(K)_4.89 //
children.translated_text: for the wealth-gathering of the virtuous is for the sake of giving, like that of rain clouds. // Ragh(K)_4.89 //
At the end of the sacrificial session, the scion of <s>Kakutstha</s>, accompanied by his ministers and friends, with great honors that assuaged the humiliation of their defeat,
permitted the kings, whose wives longed for them after the long separation, to return to their own cities. // Ragh(K)_4.90 //
Those kings, at their departure, prostrating themselves, made the feet of the emperor — marked with the signs of line, banner, pitcher, and parasol, obtainable only through his grace —
pale with the pollen-dust of <s>Makaranda</s> flowers fallen from the garlands on their crowns as they touched his toes. // Ragh(K)_4.91 //

body.translated_text: || Thus ends the fourth <s>Sarga</s> in the great poem <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s>. ||

children.translated_text: To that king, who in the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice had given away the entire contents of his treasury,

children.text: upāttavidyo gurudakṣiṇārthī kautsaḥ prapede varatantuśiṣyaḥ // Ragh(K)_5.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kautsa</s>, a pupil of <s>Varatantu</s>, who had completed his studies and sought to pay his <s>guru-dakṣiṇā</s> (preceptor's fee), came for refuge. // Ragh(K)_5.1 //
He of priceless character, placing the <s>arghya</s> (welcome-offering) in an earthen vessel — the golden one being gone —
illustrious through his fame as through his learning, that finest of hosts went forth to receive the guest. // Ragh(K)_5.2 //
Having honored him duly according to prescribed rites, the lord of men, knower of proper conduct, foremost in the wealth of respect,
joined his palms and, skilled in discerning the purpose of a visit, addressed the ascetic rich in <s>tapas</s> (austerity) who was seated on the grass seat: // Ragh(K)_5.3 //
"O keen-witted one, is your <s>Guru</s>, the foremost among the seers who composed the sacred hymns, well —
he from whom you have obtained all knowledge, as consciousness is obtained by the initiated from the fierce (<s>Ugra</s>) deity? // Ragh(K)_5.4 //

children.text: kāyena vācā manasā ca taptaṃ yadvajriṇo dhairyaviparyayāya /
children.translated_text: That threefold <s>tapas</s> of the great sage, performed with body, speech, and mind, which would cause dismay even to <s>Indra</s>'s resolve —

children.text: āpādyate na vyayamantarāyaiḥ kaccinmaharṣestrividhaṃ tapastat // Ragh(K)_5.5 //
children.translated_text: is it not being diminished by obstacles that cause loss? // Ragh(K)_5.5 //
Those hermitage trees that relieve your toil, nurtured like sons with efforts beginning with the binding of their bases —
are they not afflicted by calamities of wind and such? // Ragh(K)_5.6 //
Are the births of the does — who out of affection are not denied even the <s>Kuśa</s> grass needed for rituals — wholesome,
with lotus-stalks fallen from the lap-beds (of the sages who tend them)? // Ragh(K)_5.7 //
Are those holy waters of the <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred fords) auspicious — from which the ritual bath of observances is performed,
and from which water-oblations are offered to the ancestors — their sandbars marked by the sixth-part gleaning offering? // Ragh(K)_5.8 //
Your forest-produce — the wild rice and such, the sustenance of the body, the timely portion due to guests —
is it not pilfered by the <s>Kaḍaṅgara</s> birds and country-folk? // Ragh(K)_5.9 //

children.text: api prasannena maharṣiṇā tvaṃ samyagvinīyānumato gṛhāya /
children.translated_text: Has the great sage, being pleased, duly instructed you and given you leave to enter the householder's life?

children.text: kālo hyayaṃ saṅkramituṃ dvitīyaṃ sarvopakārakṣamamāśramaṃ te // Ragh(K)_5.10 //
children.translated_text: For this is the time for you to proceed to the second <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), which is capable of serving all. // Ragh(K)_5.10 //

children.text: tavārhato nābhigamena tṛptaṃ mano niyogakriyayotsukaṃ me /
children.translated_text: My mind, though not satisfied merely by your visit, is eager to fulfill your command;

children.text: apyājñayā śāsiturātmanā vā prāpto 'si sambhāvayituṃ vanānmām // Ragh(K)_5.11 //
children.translated_text: have you come by the order of your master, or of your own accord, to honor me from the forest?" // Ragh(K)_5.11 //
Hearing this generous speech of <s>Raghu</s>, whose depleted state was inferred from the <s>arghya</s> vessel,

children.text: svārthopapattiṃ prati durbalāśaḥ pratyāha kautsastamapetakutsam // Ragh(K)_5.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kautsa</s>, feeble in hope regarding the fulfillment of his purpose, replied to that blameless one: // Ragh(K)_5.12 //

children.text: sarvatra no vārttamavaihi rājannāthe kutastvayyaśubhaṃ prajānām /
children.translated_text: "Know that all is well with us everywhere, O king; for how could there be misfortune for the people when you are their protector?

children.text: sūrye tapatyāvaraṇāya dṛṣṭeḥ kalpeta lokasya kathaṃ tamisrā // Ragh(K)_5.13 //
children.translated_text: When the sun shines, how could darkness serve as an obstruction to sight? // Ragh(K)_5.13 //
Your devotion, befitting your lineage, toward those worthy of regard surpasses your great forebears;
but I, having come at the wrong time, approaching you as a supplicant — that is my sorrow. // Ragh(K)_5.14 //
Remaining with only your person, O lord of men, you who have given away your wealth at the sacred rite do not shine —
like a wild rice stalk remaining as a mere stump after its fruit has been gathered by forest-dwellers. // Ragh(K)_5.15 //

children.text: sthāne bhavānekanarādhipaḥ san akiñcanatvaṃ makhajaṃ vyanakti /
children.translated_text: It is fitting that you, though sole sovereign over many kings, reveal your poverty born of sacrifice;

children.text: paryāyapītasya surairhimāṃśoḥ kalākṣayaḥ ślāghyataro hi vṛddheḥ // Ragh(K)_5.16 //
children.translated_text: for the waning of the moon, sipped in turn by the gods, is more praiseworthy than its waxing. // Ragh(K)_5.16 //
Therefore I shall endeavor to obtain my <s>Guru</s>'s fee from another source, having no other purpose;

children.text: svastyastu te nirgalitāmbugarbhaṃ śaradghanaṃ nārdati cātako 'pi // Ragh(K)_5.17 //
children.translated_text: fare you well — even the <s>Cātaka</s> bird does not cry out to a cloud that has shed all its water." // Ragh(K)_5.17 //
Having spoken thus, the king detained the sage's pupil who wished to depart,

children.text: kiṃ vastu vidvangurave pradeyaṃ tvayā kiyadveti tamanvayuṅkta // Ragh(K)_5.18 //
children.translated_text: and asked him: "What is the thing to be given to your <s>Guru</s>, O learned one, and how much?" // Ragh(K)_5.18 //
Then, to that king who had duly performed the sacrifice, who was free from pride and agitation,

children.text: varṇāśramāṇāṃ gurave sa varṇī vicakṣaṇaḥ prastutamācacakṣe // Ragh(K)_5.19 //
children.translated_text: that discerning student, the guide of the <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>, related the matter at hand: // Ragh(K)_5.19 //
"Having completed my studies, I informed the great sage about the <s>guru-dakṣiṇā</s> (preceptor's fee);

children.text: sa me cirādaskhalitopacārāṃ tāṃ bhaktimevāgaṇayatpurastāt // Ragh(K)_5.20 //
children.translated_text: he, for a long time, counted only my unwavering devotion as foremost, and asked for nothing more. // Ragh(K)_5.20 //
Then, angered by my insistence, without considering my poverty, the <s>Guru</s> said to me:

children.text: vittasya vidyāparisaṅkhyayā me koṭīścatasro daśa cāhareti // Ragh(K)_5.21 //
children.translated_text: 'Bring me fourteen <s>koṭis</s> (one hundred and forty million coins), reckoned according to the branches of knowledge.' // Ragh(K)_5.21 //
I, knowing you to be one worthy of homage yet remaining a king in name only,
do not presume to importune you now, since the ransom for my learning is no small amount." // Ragh(K)_5.22 //
Thus informed by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the foremost among knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Raghu</s>, resplendent as a king among the twice-born,
whose senses were withdrawn from sin, spoke again to him, the sole lord of the world: // Ragh(K)_5.23 //
"Let it not become an occasion for reproach against me that one seeking his <s>Guru</s>'s fee, a supplicant who has seen the far shore of learning,

children.text: gato vadanyāntaramityayaṃ me mā bhūtparīvādanavāvatāraḥ // Ragh(K)_5.24 //
children.translated_text: departed from <s>Raghu</s>'s presence with his wish unfulfilled, and went to seek another generous patron. // Ragh(K)_5.24 //

children.text: sa tvaṃ prayaste mahito madīye vasaṃścaturtho 'gnirivāgnyagāre /
children.translated_text: You, being honored, please stay in my abode as a fourth fire, as it were, in a fire-sanctuary;
be patient for two or three days, O worthy one, until I can procure what you need." // Ragh(K)_5.25 //
"So be it" — trusting his unfailing word, the noble-born one accepted the agreement;

children.text: gāmāttasārāṃ raghurapyavekṣya niṣkraṣṭumarthaṃ cakame kuverāt // Ragh(K)_5.26 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Raghu</s>, seeing the earth drained of its wealth, resolved to extract riches from <s>Kubera</s>. // Ragh(K)_5.26 //
By the power born of the consecration with mantras of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, across oceans, skies, and mountains,

children.text: marutsakhasyeva balāhakasya gatirvijaghne na hi tadrathasya // Ragh(K)_5.27 //
children.translated_text: the course of his chariot was unimpeded, like that of a cloud befriended by the wind (<s>Marut</s>). // Ragh(K)_5.27 //

children.text: athādhiśiśye prayataḥ pradoṣe rathaṃ raghuḥ kalpitamastragarbham /
children.translated_text: Then at nightfall, the resolute <s>Raghu</s>, purified, mounted his chariot loaded with weapons,

children.text: sāmantasambhāvanayaiva dhīraḥ kailāsanāthaṃ tarasā jigīṣuḥ // Ragh(K)_5.28 //
children.translated_text: intending to swiftly conquer the lord of <s>Kailāsa</s>, confident even in the mere acknowledgment of his neighboring kings. // Ragh(K)_5.28 //
At dawn, to him who was facing departure, attendants arrived with amazement and joy to report

children.text: hiraṇmayīṃ kośagṛhasya madhye vṛṣṭiṃ śaśaṃsuḥ patitāṃ nabhastaḥ // Ragh(K)_5.29 //
children.translated_text: that in the middle of the treasury a rain of gold had fallen from the sky. // Ragh(K)_5.29 //
That king bestowed upon <s>Kautsa</s> the entire radiant heap of gold obtained from <s>Kubera</s>, who was about to be attacked,

children.text: dideśa kautsāya samagrameva pādaṃ sumeroriva vajrabhinnam // Ragh(K)_5.30 //
children.translated_text: in its entirety, like a peak of <s>Sumeru</s> split by the thunderbolt. // Ragh(K)_5.30 //
For the people of <s>Sāketa</s> (Ayodhyā), both of those two were worthy of celebration for their noble character;
The supplicant was free from desire beyond what the guru prescribed, and the king was more generous than the supplicant's wish demanded. // Ragh(K)_5.31 //
Then the wise <s>Kautsa</s>, pleased in mind, having received the wealth carried by hundreds of she-camels and male camels, about to depart,
touching with his hand the king whose front body was bowed, spoke these words to the lord of the people: // Ragh(K)_5.32 //
What wonder is it here if the <s>Kāmadhenu</s> (wish-fulfilling cow) should be the earth of a king who stands firm in righteousness and rules his subjects?

children.text: acintanīyastava tu prabhāvo manīṣitaṃ dyaurapi yena dugdhā // Ragh(K)_5.33 //
children.translated_text: But your power is beyond thought, by which even heaven was milked of what you desired. // Ragh(K)_5.33 //
To wish you anything else would be redundant, for all blessings have already come to you.

children.text: putraṃ labhasvātmaguṇānurūpaṃ bhavantamīḍyo bhavataḥ piteva // Ragh(K)_5.34 //
children.translated_text: May you obtain a son worthy of your own virtues — one whom the praiseworthy shall revere as they revere you, his father. // Ragh(K)_5.34 //

children.text: itthaṃ prayujyāśiṣamagryajanmā rājñe pratīyāya guroḥ sakāśam /
children.translated_text: Having thus bestowed his blessing, the twice-born sage returned to his guru's presence,

children.text: rājāpi lebhe sutamāśu tasmād ālokamarkādiva jīvalokaḥ // Ragh(K)_5.35 //
children.translated_text: and the king too swiftly obtained a son from that blessing, as the world of the living receives light from the sun. // Ragh(K)_5.35 //

children.text: brāhme muhūrte kila tasya devī kumārakalpaṃ suṣuve kumāram /
children.translated_text: At the <s>brāhma muhūrta</s> (the auspicious pre-dawn hour), his queen gave birth to a prince resplendent as a young god,

children.text: ataḥ pitā brahmaṇa eva nāmnā tamagryajanmānamajaṃ cakāra // Ragh(K)_5.36 //
children.translated_text: and so his father, by the name of <s>Brahmā</s> himself, named that firstborn <s>Aja</s> (the Unborn). // Ragh(K)_5.36 //

children.text: rūpaṃ tadojasvi tadeva vīryaṃ tadeva naisargikamunnatatvam /
children.translated_text: The same splendid form, the same valor, the same innate loftiness —

children.text: na kāraṇātsvādbibhide kumāraḥ pravartito dīpa iva pradīpāt // Ragh(K)_5.37 //
children.translated_text: the prince did not differ from his source, like a lamp lit from another lamp. // Ragh(K)_5.37 //
Him, who had duly acquired learning from his teachers, who was especially beautiful with the onset of youth,

children.text: śrīḥ kāmayānāpi guroranujñāṃ dhīreva kanyā piturācakāṅkṣa // Ragh(K)_5.38 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune), though desiring him, awaited the guru's permission like a modest maiden awaiting her father's consent. // Ragh(K)_5.38 //
Then, by the lord of the <s>Krathakaiśika</s> people, for the <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice ceremony) of his sister <s>Indumatī</s>,

children.text: āptaḥ kumārānayanotsukena bhojena dūto raghave visṛṣṭaḥ // Ragh(K)_5.39 //
children.translated_text: a trusted envoy was sent by <s>Bhoja</s>, eager to bring the prince, to <s>Raghu</s>. // Ragh(K)_5.39 //

children.text: taṃ ślāghyasambandhamasau vicintya dārakriyāyogyadaśaṃ ca putram /
children.translated_text: Considering this a praiseworthy alliance, and his son having reached the age fit for marriage,
he dispatched him with an army to the prosperous capital of the lord of <s>Vidarbha</s>. // Ragh(K)_5.40 //
Along the way, the people of the provinces, repaying favors to those who had favored them, and fruitful in their tributes,
provided halting places for the prince that were like pleasure-gardens. // Ragh(K)_5.41 //
On the bank of the <s>Narmadā</s>, where breezes moist with spray set the banners dancing,
he who had traversed the road encamped his army, whose yoked horses were foaming with exertion. // Ragh(K)_5.42 //
Then, his entry into the water heralded in advance by bees buzzing above him,
a wild elephant, his temple-walls cleansed of ichor to spotless brightness, emerged from the river. // Ragh(K)_5.43 //
With his pair of tusks, blunted against rocks, displaying on the banks of <s>Ṛkṣavat</s> mountain the appearance of a rampart,
pale-tawny with vertical blue streaks, the ochre washed away by the flood — // Ragh(K)_5.44 //
with his trunk, swift in its sweeping and contracting motions, facing the bank, noisily

children.text: babhau sa bhindansahasā taraṅgānvāryargalābhaṅga iva pravṛttaḥ // Ragh(K)_5.45 //
children.translated_text: he shone, cleaving the waves with sudden force, as if engaged in breaking water-bolts. // Ragh(K)_5.45 //
Dragging the <s>śevāla</s> (water-weed) creepers, expert in the water, pulling the delicate water-garlands — bathing-girdles of <s>Pulinda</s> women — left behind by <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks,
and trailing those that clung to his underbelly, he clambered up the bank. // Ragh(K)_5.46 //
On the temple-walls of that solitary elephant, the splendor of his rut, which had calmed for but a moment during his plunge into the pool,
blazed forth again at the sight of the many other domesticated elephants. // Ragh(K)_5.47 //
Smelling his rut-scent, unbearable with its acrid flow like the sap of the <s>saptacchada</s> tree,
the army elephants, despite violent efforts by their riders, turned away in retreat. // Ragh(K)_5.48 //
In an instant, he made the encampment tumultuous — yoke-teams scattered with broken harnesses, chariots overturned with shattered axles,
and warriors bewildered, unable to protect the women. // Ragh(K)_5.49 //
The prince, having heard that a wild elephant was inviolable to the king, as it charged forward,
struck it on the frontal globe with an arrow, his bow drawn but not excessively, intending to turn it back. // Ragh(K)_5.50 //
The moment it was struck, it shed its elephant form — to the astonishment of the watching army —
and assumed a beautiful celestial body, radiant within a halo of light, moving through the sky. // Ragh(K)_5.51 //
Then, showering the prince with flowers from wish-fulfilling trees, brought forth by his own supernatural power,
the eloquent one, whose pearl necklace on his chest was enhanced by the luster of his teeth, spoke: // Ragh(K)_5.52 //
"Due to a curse from the sage <s>Mataṅga</s>, rooted in my arrogance, I obtained the state of an elephant.

children.text: avaihi gandharvapatestanūjaṃ priyaṃvadaṃ māṃ priyadarśanasya // Ragh(K)_5.53 //
children.translated_text: Know me to be <s>Priyaṃvada</s>, son of the <s>Gandharva</s> lord <s>Priyadarśana</s>. // Ragh(K)_5.53 //
That great sage, later propitiated by me with humble bowing, became mild,
for heat comes from contact with fire and sunlight, but coolness is the natural quality of water. // Ragh(K)_5.54 //
'When <s>Aja</s>, born of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage, shall strike your frontal globe with an iron arrow,

children.text: saṃyokṣyase svena punarmahimnā tadetyavocatsa taponidhirmām // Ragh(K)_5.55 //
children.translated_text: you shall be reunited with your own splendor' — thus spoke that treasury of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) to me. // Ragh(K)_5.55 //

children.text: sa mocitaḥ śāpakalestvayāhaṃ gatiṃ prapanno vihitāṃ vidhātrā /
children.translated_text: I have been freed by you from the term of my curse and have attained the destiny ordained by the Creator.

children.text: pratikriyāṃ cedbhavato na kuryāṃ vyarthā hi me syātsvapadopalabdhiḥ // Ragh(K)_5.56 //
children.translated_text: If I should not make a return offering to you, my recovery of my own station would be in vain. // Ragh(K)_5.56 //
Therefore accept this <s>Gāndharva</s> weapon, whose <s>mantra</s> is divided into deployment and withdrawal,

children.text: prasvāpanaṃ nāma yataḥ praharturna cārihiṃsā vijayaśca haste // Ragh(K)_5.57 //
children.translated_text: called <s>Prasvāpana</s> (the Sleep-inducing), by which the wielder achieves victory without harming the enemy. // Ragh(K)_5.57 //

children.text: alaṃ hriyā māṃ prati yanmuhūrtaṃ dayāparo 'bhūḥ praharannapi tvam /
children.translated_text: Enough of modesty toward me — for even while striking, you were, for that moment, moved by compassion.

children.text: tasmādupacchandayati prayojyaṃ mayi tvayā na pratiṣedharaukṣyam // Ragh(K)_5.58 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, let me entreat you to accept what is offered; do not show the harshness of refusal toward me." // Ragh(K)_5.58 //

children.text: tathetyupaspṛśya payaḥ pavitraṃ somodbhavāyāḥ sarito nṛsomaḥ /
children.translated_text: Saying "So be it," that moon among men, having sipped the purifying water of the river born from <s>Soma</s>,
facing north, received the <s>astra</s>-<s>mantra</s> (weapon-spell) from that master of weapons, with disciplined composure. // Ragh(K)_5.59 //
Thus, by a stroke of destiny on the road, those two formed a friendship of inconceivable cause,
and one departed for the <s>Caitraratha</s> regions, while the other went on to <s>Vidarbha</s>, lovely with good governance. // Ragh(K)_5.60 //
When he stood at the outskirts of the city, the lord of the <s>Krathakaiśika</s> people, his joy swelling at that arrival,
came forth to meet him, as the ocean with its cresting waves rises to greet the moon. // Ragh(K)_5.61 //
Leading him first into the city, he attended upon him with such humility despite his own proud majesty,

children.text: mene yathā tatra janaḥ sameto vaidarbhamāgantumajaṃ gṛheśam // Ragh(K)_5.62 //
children.translated_text: that the assembled people there thought <s>Aja</s>, the guest, to be the master of <s>Vidarbha</s>'s house. // Ragh(K)_5.62 //
The lodging assigned by the king's officers with reverence — with golden vessels placed upon the altar before its eastern entrance,

children.text: ramyāṃ raghupratinidhiḥ sa navopakāryāṃ bālyātparāmiva daśāṃ madano 'dhitasthau // Ragh(K)_5.63 //
children.translated_text: that beautiful, newly furnished guest-quarter — the scion of <s>Raghu</s>, like <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) entering a stage of life beyond boyhood, took his place in it. // Ragh(K)_6.63 //
There, where the royal assembly had gathered for the <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice ceremony), that crest-jewel among maidens being the prize <s>Aja</s> longed to win,

children.text: bhāvāvabodhakaluṣā dayiteva rātrau nidrā cireṇa nayanābhimukhī babhūva // Ragh(K)_5.64 //
children.translated_text: sleep, like a beloved clouded by awareness of his heart's emotions, came before his eyes only after a long time that night. // Ragh(K)_5.64 //
Him, whose broad shoulders were pressed by his ear-ornaments, whose body-unguent had thinned from friction against the bed coverlet,
the bards awakened at dawn with charming verses in graceful meters, as one rouses the early-waking sun: // Ragh(K)_5.65 //

children.text: rātrirgatā matimatāṃ vara muñca śayyāṃ dhātrā dvidhaiva jagato nanu dhūrvibhaktā /
children.translated_text: "The night has passed, O best of the wise — leave your bed! Has not the Creator divided the world's burden in two?
On one side your guru bears it with tireless vigilance; on the other, you are the one who takes up the yoke. // Ragh(K)_5.66 //

children.text: nidrāvaśena bhavatā hyanavekṣyamāṇā paryutsukatvamabalā niśi khaṇḍiteva /
children.translated_text: Unattended by you in your power of sleep, <s>Lakṣmī</s> (the goddess of fortune), like a neglected woman at night, grows restless,

children.text: lakṣmīrvinodayati yena digantalambī so 'pi tvadānanarucaṃ vijahāti candraḥ // Ragh(K)_5.67 //
children.translated_text: and even the moon, who delights her as he hangs at the horizon's edge, abandons the beauty of your face. // Ragh(K)_5.67 //

children.text: tadvalgunā yugapadunmiṣitena tāvat sadyaḥ parasparatulāmadhirohatāṃ dve /
children.translated_text: Therefore, with that graceful opening of both eyes at once, let two things at that instant mount the scale of mutual comparison —
your eye, with its slightly trembling and otherwise rough-textured iris, and the lotus, with its stirring bee within. // Ragh(K)_5.68 //
The dawn breeze, as if desiring the natural fragrance of the breath from your mouth, carries off flowers loosened from their stalks on the <s>Anokahā</s> trees,

children.text: svābhāvikaṃ paraguṇena vibhātavātaḥ saugandhyamīpsuriva te mukhamārutasya // Ragh(K)_5.69 //
children.translated_text: and mingles them with lotuses split open by the red rays of dawn. // Ragh(K)_5.69 //
The dew-drops fallen upon the reddish undersides of tree-leaves, clear as washed pearl beads,

children.text: saṃlakṣyate daśanacandrikayānuviddhaṃ bimboṣṭhalabdhaparabhāgamiva smitaṃ te // Ragh(K)_5.70 //
children.translated_text: pierced by the moonlight of your teeth, appear like your smile that has gained superiority over your <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips. // Ragh(K)_5.70 //

children.text: yāvatpratāpanidhirākramate na bhānurahnāya tāvadaruṇena tamo nirastam /
children.translated_text: Before the sun, that repository of valor, advances to seize the day, darkness has been dispelled by <s>Aruṇa</s> (the dawn).

children.text: āyodhanāgrasaratāṃ tvayi vīra yāte kiṃ vā ripūṃstava guruḥ svayamucchinatti // Ragh(K)_5.71 //
children.translated_text: When you, O hero, go forth to the front of battle, does your guru himself destroy the enemies? // Ragh(K)_5.71 //
Your war-elephants, who have slept lightly on both flanks, leave their resting places, dragging their clanking chains.

children.text: yeṣāṃ vibhānti taruṇāruṇarāgayogādbhinnādrigairikataṭā iva dantakośāḥ // Ragh(K)_5.72 //
children.translated_text: Their tusk-sheaths gleam with the color of fresh dawn-red, like mountain cliffs smeared with red ochre. // Ragh(K)_5.72 //

children.text: dīrgheṣvamī niyamitāḥ paṭamaṇḍapeṣu nidrāṃ vidhūya vanajākṣa vanāyujāste /
children.translated_text: Your horses, stabled in long tent-pavilions, O lotus-eyed one, shaking off sleep,

children.text: vaktroṣmaṇā malinayanti purogatāni lehyāni saindhavaśilāśakalāni vāhāḥ // Ragh(K)_5.73 //
children.translated_text: those steeds, with the warmth of their breath, moisten the pieces of rock-salt placed before them as they lick them. // Ragh(K)_5.73 //
The lamps grow sparse in their offerings, their flower-decorations wilted, empty of the halo-burst of their rays.

children.text: ayamapi ca giraṃ nastvatprabodhaprayuktāmanuvadati śukaste mañjuvākpañjarasthaḥ // Ragh(K)_5.74 //
children.translated_text: And this parrot of yours, dwelling in his sweet-voiced cage, echoes back our words that are meant to rouse you. // Ragh(K)_5.74 //

children.text: iti sa vihṛtanidrastalpamalpetarāṃsaḥ suragaja iva gāṅgaṃ saikataṃ supratīkaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus he, having shaken off sleep from his couch, broad-shouldered, handsome as the divine elephant <s>Supratīka</s> on the sandy bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
released the coverlet's edge, bitten by the jewels of the bracelets of the attendant women busy at his feet. // Ragh(K)_5.75 //
Then, having completed the rites prescribed by scripture, appropriate for the morning, with elegantly arched eyelashes,
dressed in attire skillfully arranged to suit the occasion, he went to the assembly of kings gathered for the <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice ceremony). // Ragh(K)_5.76 //

body.translated_text: || Thus ends the fifth <s>sarga</s> (canto) in the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem). ||

children.translated_text: There, upon platforms rivaling celestial chariots, he beheld kings seated on thrones, their beauty enhanced by full adornment,
like sacrificial posts freshly anointed upon golden altars. // Ragh(K)_6.1 //
When the kings beheld the scion of <s>Kakutstha</s>, as though the god of love, having granted their courtship its due,
had then reclaimed his own body from the lord, their minds became despairing of winning <s>Indumatī</s>. // Ragh(K)_6.2 //
Then the prince, directed by the lord of <s>Vidarbha</s>, ascended the lofty platform by a prepared stairway,
like a young lion ascending the high lap of a mountain by rocky ledges. // Ragh(K)_6.3 //
He took his seat upon a jewel-studded throne furnished with a coverlet of surpassing color,
and was, for the most part, of incomparable beauty — like <s>Guha</s> (Kārttikeya) resting upon the back of a peacock. // Ragh(K)_6.4 //
Among those royal lineages arrayed in splendor, he, difficult to gaze upon due to the extraordinary rise of his radiance,

children.text: sahasradhātmā vyarucadvibhaktaḥ payomucāṃ paṅktiṣu vidyuteva // Ragh(K)_6.5 //
children.translated_text: shone forth — the self distributed thousandfold — like lightning amid rows of clouds. // Ragh(K)_6.5 //
Among those kings who occupied costly thrones and wore magnificent attire, the son of <s>Raghu</s>

children.text: rarāja dhāmnā raghusūnureva kalpadrumāṇāmiva pārijātaḥ // Ragh(K)_6.6 //
children.translated_text: alone shone resplendent in his glory, like the <s>Pārijāta</s> among wish-fulfilling trees. // Ragh(K)_6.6 //
The throngs of eyes of the townspeople abandoned all the other kings and fell upon him,

children.text: madotkaṭe recitapuṣpavṛkṣā gandhadvipe vanya iva dvirephāḥ // Ragh(K)_6.7 //
children.translated_text: like wild bees, forsaking flowering trees, drawn to a fragrant elephant in rut. // Ragh(K)_6.7 //
Then, when the bards versed in lineage praised the solar and lunar dynasties among the assembly of kings,
when incense from <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) essence was wafted about, its smoke-spirals perfuming the banners, // Ragh(K)_6.8 //
when the cause of excited dancing among the peacocks dwelling in the groves near the city arose,

children.text: pradhmātaśaṅkhe parito digantāṃstūryasvane mūrchati maṅgalārthe // Ragh(K)_6.9 //
children.translated_text: when the conch was blown and the auspicious sound of instruments swelled to fill the horizons on every side, // Ragh(K)_6.9 //
she who would choose her lord, radiant amid her maiden retinue, mounting a palanquin borne by men, fit to traverse the four quarters,
entered the royal avenue between the platforms, dressed in attire mingled with festive ornament. // Ragh(K)_6.10 //
Upon that extraordinary creation of the Creator — that maiden who was the target of a thousand eyes —
the kings fell with their inner selves, while remaining with their bodies merely seated on their thrones. // Ragh(K)_6.11 //
Toward her, various amorous gestures of the kings whose desires had become manifest served as the first messengers of their love,

children.text: pravātaśobhā iva pādapānāṃ śṛṅgāraceṣṭā vividhā babhūvuḥ // Ragh(K)_6.12 //
children.translated_text: like the beauty of trees swaying in the breeze. // Ragh(K)_6.12 //
One king twirled between his hands a playful lotus, its stem clasped tight, its swaying petals striking the bees away,
its interior made beautiful by pollen-dust. // Ragh(K)_6.13 //
Another, a man of refined grace, his upper garment having slipped from his shoulder, momentarily caught on the edge of his armlet,
lifted it back to its proper place, his handsome face turned aside. // Ragh(K)_6.14 //
Yet another, with fingertips curled, his eye-beauty slightly drawn inward in concentration,

children.text: ratnāṃśusampṛktanakhaprabheṇa pādena haimaṃ vililekha pīṭham // Ragh(K)_6.15 //
children.translated_text: with his foot, its nail-luster mingled with the radiance of gems, scratched upon the golden footstool. // Ragh(K)_6.15 //
Another, resting his left arm upon the edge of his seat, its armlet pressed tight against his side,
his necklace parted as his torso twisted, became absorbed in conversation with a friend. // Ragh(K)_6.16 //
Another young man took a pale <s>ketaka</s> (screwpine) feather — like a coquette's fan of tooth-marks —
and with his fingertips, in strokes suited to a beloved's hip, split it apart. // Ragh(K)_6.17 //
One [king], with a hand copper-red as a lotus petal, marked with the emblem of lines and banners,
playfully rolled the dice, pierced through by the radiance of his blazing rings. [Ragh(K) 6.18]
Another, though seated in his proper place, as if his own position were transgressing [its bounds],
busied one hand upon his crown, through the aperture between fingers pregnant with diamond-light. [Ragh(K) 6.19]
Then <s>Sunandā</s>, the guardian of the gate, bold as a man, knowing the lineage and conduct of kings by report,
having first led the princess near to the lord of <s>Magadha</s>, spoke: [Ragh(K) 6.20]
"This is the refuge of those eager for protection, of unfathomable inner strength, the foundation of <s>Magadha</s>,

children.text: rājā prajārañjanalabdhavarṇaḥ parantapo nāma yathārthanāmā // Ragh(K)_6.21 //
children.translated_text: the king named <s>Parantapa</s> (Scorcher of Foes), whose name is true to its meaning, who has earned his title by gladdening his subjects. [Ragh(K) 6.21]

children.text: kāmaṃ nṛpāḥ santi sahasrasaṅkhyā rājanvatīmāhuranena pṛthvīm /
children.translated_text: Though kings exist in thousands, the earth is said to have a [true] king because of him alone,
just as the night, though crowded with stars and planets, is luminous only because of the moon. [Ragh(K) 6.22]
Through the unbroken series of his sacrificial rites, he who perpetually invites the thousand-eyed one (<s>Indra</s>),
has long made the temple-curls of <s>Śacī</s>, pale-cheeked [from longing], bereft of <s>Mandāra</s> flowers. [Ragh(K) 6.23]

children.text: anena cedicchasi gṛhyamāṇaṃ pāṇiṃ vareṇyena kuru praveśe /
children.translated_text: If you wish your hand to be taken by this most worthy one, make an entrance
that is a feast for the eyes of the women of <s>Puṣpapura</s> (Pāṭaliputra), who lean upon the palace windows." [Ragh(K) 6.24]
When she had spoken thus about him, the slender one, glancing at him slightly, her garland of <s>madhūka</s> flowers with its <s>dūrvā</s> grass slightly slipping,
rejected him without speaking, through the mere act of a straight bow. [Ragh(K) 6.25]

children.text: tāṃ sātha vetragrahaṇe niyuktā rājāntaraṃ rājasutāṃ nināya /
children.translated_text: Then the rod-bearer (<s>Sunandā</s>) led that princess to another king,
like a wave-line driven by the wind leading a royal swan of <s>Mānasa</s> lake from one lotus to another. [Ragh(K) 6.26]
And she said of him: "This lord of women, whose youthful beauty is sought even by celestial women,

children.text: vinītabhāgaḥ kila sūtrakārairaindraṃ padaṃ bhūmigato 'pi bhuṅkte // Ragh(K)_6.27 //
children.translated_text: though dwelling on earth, enjoys the rank of <s>Indra</s>, assigned to him, they say, by the lawgivers (<s>sūtrakāras</s>). [Ragh(K) 6.27]
By him, tear-drops as large as pearls have been shed upon the breasts
of his enemies' women — necklaces returned, as it were, without the thread of reproach. [Ragh(K) 6.28]
<s>Śrī</s> (fortune) and <s>Sarasvatī</s> (learning), naturally dwelling in different abodes, reside together in him;

children.text: kāntyā girā sūnṛtayā ca yogyā tvameva kalyāṇi tayostṛtīyā // Ragh(K)_6.29 //
children.translated_text: you, O auspicious one, by beauty, speech, and truthfulness, are the fitting third to those two. [Ragh(K) 6.29]"
Then, lowering her eyes from the king of <s>Aṅga</s>, the princess said 'Proceed' to the attendants;

children.text: nāsau na kāmyo na ca veda samyag draṣṭuṃ na sā bhinnarucirhi lokaḥ // Ragh(K)_6.30 //
children.translated_text: it was not that he was not desirable, nor that she did not know how to look properly — for the world is of varied tastes. [Ragh(K) 6.30]

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ duṣprasahaṃ pareṣāṃ nṛpaṃ niyuktā pratihārabhūmau /
children.translated_text: Then, the one appointed to the role of usher showed the princess a king irresistible to foes,
of exceptional beauty — like the newly risen moon to <s>Indumatī</s>. [Ragh(K) 6.31]
"This lord of <s>Avantī</s>, with upraised arms, broad-chested and slender-waisted,
glows as if sketched by the instrument of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> (the divine craftsman), having mounted the wheel's rotation of blazing splendor. [Ragh(K) 6.32]
During his marches, the dust raised by the horses running before him at full strength
eclipses the luster-rays of the crest-jewels of [his] feudatory kings. [Ragh(K) 6.33]
Dwelling near the temple of <s>Mahākāla</s>, whose crest is a half-moon,

children.text: divāpi jālāntaracandrikāṇāṃ nārīsakhaḥ sparśasukhāni bhuṅkte // Ragh(K)_6.34 //
children.translated_text: even by day, this friend of women enjoys the delight of moonbeams streaming through latticed windows. [Ragh(K) 6.34]

children.text: anena yūnā saha pārthivena rambhoru kaccinmanaso ruciste /
children.translated_text: O one of plantain-like thighs, is your heart inclined to sport with this young king
in the succession of gardens, whose trees tremble in the breeze from the waves of the <s>Siprā</s>? [Ragh(K) 6.35]"
Even upon him, a resplendent image of beauty, whose foes' [pride] was dried up by his valor,

children.text: babandha sā nottamasaukumāryā kumudvatī bhānumatīva bhāvam // Ragh(K)_6.36 //
children.translated_text: she of the most exquisite delicacy did not fix her affection — like the night-lotus (<s>kumudvatī</s>) upon the full sun (<s>bhānumatī</s>). [Ragh(K) 6.36]
Passing her beyond him to one who was like [the glow between] lotuses, of the coastal king who was not lacking in qualities,

children.text: vidhāya sṛṣṭiṃ lalitāṃ vidhātur jagāda bhūyaḥ sunasāṃ sunandā // Ragh(K)_6.37 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sunandā</s>, knowing [her art], spoke again to the beautiful-nosed princess, presenting a charming creation of the Creator: [Ragh(K) 6.37]
"Whose thousand arms were accomplished in battle, whose sacrificial posts were planted in eighteen islands —

children.text: ananyasādhāraṇarājaśabdo babhūva yogī kila kārtavīryaḥ // Ragh(K)_6.38 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kārtavīrya</s>, they say, was a <s>yogī</s>, with a title of royalty shared by no other. [Ragh(K) 6.38]
And [this king], appearing before [wrongdoers] at the very moment of criminal thought, bearing his bow,

children.text: antaḥśarīreṣvapi yaḥ prajānāṃ pratyādideśāvinayaṃ vinetā // Ragh(K)_6.39 //
children.translated_text: a discipliner who checked insolence even within the bodies of his subjects. [Ragh(K) 6.39]
By whom — with his arm rigid from the pressure of the bowstring — the ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>),
defeated by <s>Indra</s>, sighing mouth after mouth, dwelt in prison until [<s>Kārtavīrya</s>'s] gracious release. [Ragh(K) 6.40]
In his lineage was born this king named <s>Pradīpa</s>, a devotee of elders versed in tradition,

children.text: yena śriyaḥ saṃśrayadoṣarūḍhaṃ svabhāvaloletyayaśaḥ pramṛṣṭam // Ragh(K)_6.41 //
children.translated_text: by whom the ill-fame — grown from the fault of sheltering <s>Śrī</s> (fortune, i.e., that she is fickle by nature) — was wiped clean. [Ragh(K) 6.41]
Who, in battle, having obtained as an ally one of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s movement — the death-night of warriors —
holds the sharp edge of <s>Rāma</s>'s (<s>Paraśurāma</s>'s) axe to be [no more than] the pith of a blue lotus petal. [Ragh(K) 6.42]
Become the fortune of this long-armed one's lap! If there is a desire to behold

children.text: prāsādajālairjalaveṇiramyāṃ revāṃ yadi prekṣitumasti kāmaḥ // Ragh(K)_6.43 //
children.translated_text: <s>Revā</s> (the Narmadā river), lovely with water-braids [visible] through the palace lattices, [her banks] girdled by the ramparts of <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>. [Ragh(K) 6.43]"

children.text: tasyāḥ prakāmapriyadarśano 'pi na sa kṣitīśo rucaye babhūva /
children.translated_text: Though he was exceedingly handsome to behold, that king did not find favor with her,
like the full moon [failing to please] the night-lotus — [the moon] whose stain of clouds is wiped clean by autumn. [Ragh(K) 6.44]
She, guarded by the inner-chamber attendants, indicated <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, the lord of the <s>Śūrasenas</s>,
whose fame was sung in distant lands, a lamp of both lineages pure in conduct — the princess spoke: [Ragh(K) 6.45]

children.text: nīpānvayaḥ pārthiva eṣa yajvā guṇairyamāśritya paraspareṇa /
children.translated_text: "This king of the <s>Nīpa</s> lineage, a performer of sacrifices — relying on whose qualities mutually,

children.text: naisargiko 'pyutsasṛje virodhaḥ siddhāśramaṃ śāntamivaitya sattvaiḥ // Ragh(K)_6.46 //
children.translated_text: even a natural enmity was released, as by wild animals entering the peaceful precincts of <s>Siddhāśrama</s>. [Ragh(K) 6.46]
In whose own body a radiance pleasing to the eye is settled, like that of the moon,
[but whose] unbearable splendor [is reflected] in the enemies' palaces, where grass sprouts grow on the rooftops. [Ragh(K) 6.47]
At the time of water-sports, from the washing of his harem-women's sandal-paste from their breasts,
the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), even as she flows past <s>Mathurā</s>, appears as if her waters were mingled with the waves of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. [Ragh(K) 6.48]

children.text: trātena tārkṣyātkila kāliyena maṇiṃ visṛṣṭaṃ yamunaukasā yaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, wearing on his broad chest the jewel released by the <s>Yamunā</s>-dwelling <s>Kāliya</s> [serpent], rescued from <s>Garuḍa</s>,

children.text: vakṣaḥsthalavyāpirucaṃ dadhānaḥ sakaustubhaṃ hrepayatīva kṛṣṇam // Ragh(K)_6.49 //
children.translated_text: whose luster spreads across his chest, puts to shame <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself along with his <s>Kaustubha</s> gem. [Ragh(K) 6.49]
Honoring this young lord as your husband, upon a couch of soft sprouts and flowers,

children.text: vṛndāvane caitrarathādanūne nirviśyatāṃ sundari yauvanaśrīḥ // Ragh(K)_6.50 //
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, let the glory of your youth be enjoyed in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, not inferior to the garden of <s>Citraratha</s>! [Ragh(K) 6.50]
And seated upon rock-ledges, wet with water-drops and covered with moss,

children.text: kalāpināṃ prāvṛṣi paśya nṛttaṃ kāntāsu govardhanakandarāsu // Ragh(K)_6.51 //
children.translated_text: behold the dance of peacocks in the rainy season, in the lovely caves of <s>Govardhana</s>! [Ragh(K) 6.51]"
She, who was to become another's bride, passed by that king too — [he who had] a navel lovely as a whirlpool —
like a river flowing toward the ocean, passing by a mountain encountered on the way. [Ragh(K) 6.52]
Then the maid-servant, approaching <s>Hemāṅgada</s> by name, the lord of <s>Kaliṅga</s>, whose arms were clasped with armlets,
who had destroyed the enemy faction, addressed the young girl with a face like the new moon: [Ragh(K) 6.53]
"This lord of <s>Mahendra</s> [mountain] and of the great ocean, whose mettle equals <s>Mahendra</s> mountain,

children.text: yasya kṣaratsainyagajacchalena yātrāsu yātīva puro mahendraḥ // Ragh(K)_6.54 //
children.translated_text: before whom, during his campaigns, <s>Mahendra</s> mountain itself seems to march, under the pretext of his streaming war-elephants. [Ragh(K) 6.54]

children.text: jyāghātalekhe subhujo bhujābhyāṃ bibharti yaścāpabhṛtāṃ purogaḥ /
children.translated_text: On his well-formed arms, marked with the lines of bowstring-strikes, the foremost of bow-bearers, he carries

children.text: ripuśriyaḥ sāñjanavāṣpaseke vandīkṛtāyā iva paddhatī dve // Ragh(K)_6.55 //
children.translated_text: what seem two paths of his enemies' fortune, [now] captive, her collyrium-tears washing [his arms]. [Ragh(K) 6.55]
The ocean itself, with rows of areca palms on the beach-shore visible through the palace lattices,
drowning out the watches-of-the-night drums with its deep sound, awakens him from sleep. [Ragh(K) 6.56]
Sport with him on the shores of the sea, where palmyra groves rustle,
your perspiration removed by breezes bearing clove-flowers from the islands beyond. [Ragh(K) 6.57]"
Though awakened [to interest], the younger sister of the <s>Vidarbha</s> king, lovely of form, by those very [words],

children.text: tasmādapāvartata pauruṣeṇa nīteva lakṣmīḥ pratikūladaivāt // Ragh(K)_6.58 //
children.translated_text: turned away from him — like <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune) led away by manly prowess from adverse fate. [Ragh(K) 6.58]
Then the doorkeeper, approaching the lord of <s>Nāgapura</s>, tall-nosed and of divine form,

children.text: itaścakorākṣi vilokayeti nāgāṅganābhāṃ nijagāda bhojyām // Ragh(K)_6.59 //
children.translated_text: spoke to the princess of <s>Nāga</s>-woman-like beauty: 'Look this way, O <s>Cakorākṣī</s> (partridge-eyed one)!' [Ragh(K) 6.59]
"This <s>Pāṇḍya</s>, with long garlands draped upon his shoulders, his body anointed with <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandal-paste),
shines like the king of mountains, its peaks reddened by the morning sun, with cascading waterfalls. [Ragh(K) 6.60]
He who arrested the great mountain <s>Vindhya</s>, who drank the ocean dry and disgorged it completely —
<s>Agastya</s>, his body moist from the concluding bath (<s>avabhṛtha</s>) of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> sacrifice, gladly becomes his bathing-companion. [Ragh(K) 6.61]
He by whom, having obtained the hard-to-get weapon from <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the arrogant lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>,

children.text: purā janasthānavimardaśaṅkī sandhāya laṅkādhipatiḥ pratasthe // Ragh(K)_6.62 //
children.translated_text: fearing an attack on <s>Janasthāna</s>, in former times made peace and set forth. [Ragh(K) 6.62]

children.text: anena pāṇau vidhivadgṛhīte mahākulīnena mahīva gurvī /
children.translated_text: With your hand duly taken by this one of great lineage, become, like the weighty earth

children.text: ratnānuviddhārṇavamekhalāyā diśaḥ sapatnī bhava dakṣiṇasyāḥ // Ragh(K)_6.63 //
children.translated_text: girdled by the gem-studded ocean, a co-wife of the southern direction! [Ragh(K) 6.63]
In the <s>Malaya</s> highlands, where betel-vines entwine the areca palms,
and <s>elā</s> (cardamom) creepers embrace the sandal trees, upon beds strewn with <s>tamāla</s> leaves,
be pleased to sport forever upon beds strewn with <s>tamāla</s> leaves! [Ragh(K) 6.64]
"This king, dark-bodied as a blue lotus, and you, of a body-stalk golden as <s>rocanā</s> —
may the union of you two be for the enhancement of each other's beauty, like lightning and a rain-cloud! [Ragh(K) 6.65]"
His instruction from her [attendant], though about the <s>Vidarbha</s> king's [family], did not find a place in her heart,

children.text: sañcāriṇī dīpaśikheva rātrau yaṃ yaṃ vyatīyāya patiṃvarā sā /
children.translated_text: like a moonbeam upon a lotus that has closed its cup at the sight of the sun. [Ragh(K) 6.66]

children.text: narendramārgāṭṭa iva prapede vivarṇabhāvaṃ sa sa bhūmipālaḥ // Ragh(K)_6.67 //
children.translated_text: Like a moving lamp-flame at night, whomever that bride-to-be passed by,

children.text: tasyāṃ raghoḥ sūnurupasthitāyāṃ vṛṇīta māṃ neti samākulo 'bhūt /
children.translated_text: that king became pale, as if passed by a highway-wayside merchant. [Ragh(K) 6.67]
When she approached the son of <s>Raghu</s>, he became agitated [thinking] 'Will she choose me or not?' —
his right arm dispelled his doubt, swelling against the armlet's clasp. [Ragh(K) 6.68]

children.text: na hi praphultaṃ sahakārametya vṛkṣāntaraṃ kāṅkṣati ṣaṭpadālī // Ragh(K)_6.69 //
children.translated_text: Reaching him who was faultless in every limb, the princess turned away from approaching any other,
for a swarm of bees, having found a fully blossomed mango, does not seek another tree. [Ragh(K) 6.69]

children.text: pracakrame vaktumanukramajñā suvistaraṃ vākyamidaṃ sunandā // Ragh(K)_6.70 //
children.translated_text: Perceiving <s>Indumatī</s>, moon-radiant, with her mind's activity fixed upon him,
<s>Sunandā</s>, knowing the proper sequence, began to speak these words at length: [Ragh(K) 6.70]

children.text: kākutsthaśabdaṃ yata unnatecchāḥ ślāghyaṃ dadhatyuttarakosalendrāḥ // Ragh(K)_6.71 //
children.translated_text: "Of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage, there was <s>Kakutstha</s>, the crest-jewel of kings, of well-earned renown;
from whom the <s>Uttarakosala</s> lords, lofty in their ambitions, proudly bear the title '<s>Kākutstha</s>.' [Ragh(K) 6.71]
He who, mounting <s>Mahendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) in the form of a great bull, having playfully assumed the role of the <s>Pināka</s>-wielder (<s>Śiva</s>) in battle,
with his arrows rendered the cheeks of <s>Asura</s> women bereft of their decorative leaf-markings. [Ragh(K) 6.72]
He who, clashing armlet against armlet with <s>Airāvaṇa</s> (Indra's elephant) — his own [armlet] loosened by the impact —

children.text: jātaḥ kule tasya kilendukīrteḥ kulapradīpo nṛpatirdilīpaḥ /
children.translated_text: mounted the half-seat of the mountain-splitter (<s>Indra</s>) himself, who had approached in his own foremost form. [Ragh(K) 6.73]
In the lineage of that one of moon-like fame was born <s>Dilīpa</s>, the lamp of the dynasty, the king

children.text: yasminmahīṃ śāsati māninīnāṃ nidrāṃ vihārārdhapathe gatānām /
children.translated_text: who stopped at ninety-nine [sacrifices] to avert <s>Śakra</s>'s (<s>Indra</s>'s) jealousy. [Ragh(K) 6.74]

children.text: vāto 'pi nāsraṃsayadaṃśukāni ko lambayedābharaṇāya hastam // Ragh(K)_6.75 //
children.translated_text: While he ruled the earth, even the wind did not displace the garments of proud women

children.text: putro raghustasya padaṃ praśāsti mahākratorviśvajitaḥ prayoktā /
children.translated_text: who had fallen asleep midway through their amorous play — who then would stretch a hand toward their ornaments? [Ragh(K) 6.75]
His son <s>Raghu</s> rules his realm, the performer of the great all-conquering sacrifice (<s>Viśvajit</s>),
who reduced to the remainder of an earthen vessel the wealth gathered from the conquest of the four directions. [Ragh(K) 6.76]

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ gataṃ yasya na cānubandhi yaśaḥ paricchettumiyattayālam // Ragh(K)_6.77 //
children.translated_text: His fame — which has ascended mountains, crossed oceans, entered the abode of serpents,
and gone upward [to heaven] — has no limit, nor can its extent be measured. [Ragh(K) 6.77]

children.text: gurvīṃ dhuraṃ yo bhuvanasya pitryāṃ dhuryeṇa damyaḥ sadṛśīṃ bibharti // Ragh(K)_6.78 //
children.translated_text: This prince is his son <s>Aja</s>, born after [his father], like <s>Jayanta</s> [born after] the lord of <s>Triviṣṭapa</s> (heaven);

children.text: kulena kāntyā vayasā navena guṇaiśca taistairvinayapradhānaiḥ /
children.translated_text: he who bears the weighty ancestral burden of the world, like a yoked draft-ox of equal capacity. [Ragh(K) 6.78]

children.text: tvamātmanastulyamimaṃ vṛṇīṣva ratnaṃ samāgacchatu kāñcanena // Ragh(K)_6.79 //
children.translated_text: By lineage, by beauty, by his fresh youth, and by qualities of every kind led by modesty —
choose him as your equal self; let the jewel be united with the gold. [Ragh(K) 6.79]"
Then, at the conclusion of <s>Sunandā</s>'s speech, the king's daughter, softening her bashfulness,

children.text: sā yūni tasminnabhilāṣabandhaṃ śaśāka śālīnatayā na vaktum /
children.translated_text: accepted the prince with a glance pure as grace — as if with a garland of betrothal (<s>saṃvaraṇasraj</s>). [Ragh(K) 6.80]

children.text: romāñcalakṣyeṇa sa gātrayaṣṭiṃ bhittvā nirākrāmadarālakeśyāḥ // Ragh(K)_6.81 //
children.translated_text: She could not speak her bond of desire for that youth, out of modesty;

children.text: tathāgatāyāṃ parihāsapūrvaṃ sakhyāṃ sakhī vetradharā babhāṣe /
children.translated_text: [but] it broke through the body-stalk of the curly-haired one, visible through the horripilation. [Ragh(K) 6.81]

children.text: ārye vrajāmo 'nyata ityathaināṃ vadhūrasūyākuṭilaṃ dadarśa // Ragh(K)_6.82 //
children.translated_text: When [<s>Sunandā</s>] thus approached, the rod-bearing friend said to [her] friend with a jest: 'Noble one, let us go elsewhere!' — and then
the bride looked at her with a glance crooked with jealous displeasure. [Ragh(K) 6.82]

children.text: āsañjayāmāsa yathāpradeśaṃ kaṇṭhe guṇaṃ mūrtamivānurāgam // Ragh(K)_6.83 //
children.translated_text: placed the garland in its proper place upon his neck — like affection made manifest. [Ragh(K) 6.83]
With that garland made of auspicious flowers, hanging down upon his broad chest,
the excellent one (<s>Aja</s>) embraced the younger sister of the <s>Vidarbha</s> king, her arms clasped around his neck. [Ragh(K) 6.84]
"The <s>kaumudī</s> (moonlight) has reached the moon; the river <s>Jāhnavī</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>) has descended into the ocean, a fitting [match] freed from clouds" —

children.text: iti samaguṇayogaprītayastatra paurāḥ śravaṇakaṭu nṛpāṇāmekavākyaṃ vivavruḥ // Ragh(K)_6.85 //
children.translated_text: thus the citizens there, delighted by the union of equal qualities, uttered in one voice [words] harsh to the ears of [the other] kings. [Ragh(K) 6.85]
On one side, the assembly of kings with the bridegroom's party rejoicing; on the other, the canopy —

children.text: uṣasi sara iva praphultapadmaṃ kumudavanapratipannanidramāsīt // Ragh(K)_6.86 //
children.translated_text: at dawn, like a lake with lotuses fully bloomed [on one side] and a grove of night-lotuses that had assumed sleep [on the other]. [Ragh(K) 6.86]

body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth <s>sarga</s> (canto) of the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem).
